analysis.name: Nicole Callihan

Professor Callihan is a great professor. She really cares about you and wants you to succeed so if you're having trouble all you have to do is go visit her and she will try and guide you. Amazing professor with a marvelous sense of humor. Extremely enthusiastic about the material and made me genuinely excited to come to class. Do not take this professor, lectures are not useful AT ALL. You will end up having to teach yourself all of the material. The class is very disorganized and she is not helpful at answering questions. Please take a different professor if you can.

review_highlights.comment: The professor is great and explains things really clearly. If English isn't your first language, definitely go to every class and preview the material beforehand. Prof. Duman is funny, but her exams are tough. Exams have multiple choice, brain labeling, true or false questions, and an essay. Took two classes w/her and she's a nice prof but the courses are pretty boring... Attendance not mandatory but you need to go to pass the exams.

Very interesting course given current events. looks like keanu reeves!! Hottttttttt!

analysis.name: Frances  Hogan

Easy A if you just pay attention and participate in class. She really cares about students, pay attention and respects their opinions, and was the first professor who remember my culture on name preference. One of the best prof and highly recommended.

analysis.name: Todd Foley

He is good but there are four papers in a semster, be ready to read different books or articals every week but it is an easy class btw. If you follow him everey week you will be fine.

Professor Foley is passionate about cinema but the course is not organized and it's hard to systematically understand Chinese cinema after this course. Please. Please. whatever you do do not take this professor. He is the most disorganised person you will ever meet. analysis.name: David Foley

You have so much homework every class that doesn't even contribute to your essay. all of the lectures are long and boring and filled with things I knew since middle school. David Foley is the worst! I was taking his class while struggling with depression and anxiety and he upped that with his confusing advice and inconsiderate attitude. He's very particular about little details that don't matter; for instance he refused to accept an essay because I didn't use the right kind of folder.  DO NOT take his class.

analysis.name: Joseph Foudy

might just be one of the worst professors at NYU literally just doing this as a job for a salary so dry and literally the most annoying style of humor i may have every come across. tests are incredibly difficult and topics emphasized in class are almost completely absent form the test and topics that are barely covered are emphasized in the exams.

analysis.name: Jacob French

literally my favorite professor ever. he's so funny and so engaging and genuinely knows what he's talking about. his class is so pleasant and honestly there is no homework, just readings and class lectures and discussions. you just get 2 essays, and a midterm and final which are in class essays.

(CORE-500 Cultures and Context - Middle Eastern Cities)

unclear grading standards and instructions, lectures focus mostly in readings and are not very helpful.

Take this class if you want your GPA to be lowered!!!!

Graded by 4 exams and attendance. Prepare with the textbook questions well to get an A in each exam. Decent curve at the end. class was in Cantor in the morning and he tends to ramble a bit, so it was really hard to stay awake. The last unit where he shows documentaries is interesting + helps, go to those. he's pretty inspiring, would recommend

Professor Catovic is chill but his lectures don't seem to be too helpful. He tends to read off slides and his exams are 25 MCQ. His course grading scheme is ambiguous and impossible to determine on your own. Found many of his exam questions to be ambiguous or unrelated to the important macroeconomic principles. HW and attendance count for 20%.

When taking good quality notes, I did learn some things in class, however it could have also been done from at home as he posts the slides online. As someone who struggles to take tests, BEWARE. You could study heavily days leading up to the exam (as I did), but his tests are designed to trick you, are worded weirdly, and make you question yourself

analysis.name: Richard Hendler
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 144 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: A legend and iconic. He is by far the best professor I have ever had in life. He knows all of the material and his lectures are amazing and fun. He develops a community, is very approachable, and creates a very safe place to learn (no fear about making mistakes; in fact he refers to those as pre-successes.  Many deliverables/readings, worth it tho.

Rich is a fantastic professor. He goes out of his way to make the class interesting, and has a ton of both legal and teaching experience to draw on. His final is tough, and he asks for your full attention on a lot of assignments, but if you want to be anywhere in the entertainment industry, his class is worth taking for sure.

E&L is the first class that genuinely feels like i'm having a conversation with an old friend (coming from someone in Gallatin). He is very talented in his delivery in that you will be engrossed in the class and he has a great personality! Very caring professor and truly wants his students to succeed. Sad I can't take more classes with him (senior)

Rich is a must-take for anyone with an interest in law or entertainment. Rich is a spectacular professor and an even better human being, His classes are very interesting and relevant. His workload is heavy, so manage your time. In the end, it as so worthwhile as I learned more than I could ever imagine and I found my passion by taking this class.

Hands down and by far the best class and professor at NYU. Rich is smart, engaging, funny, and understanding, and he managed to the get the most out of me. There is a lot of work, but all of it is very interesting. I cannot express how much I disagree with the other student in my class. I learned so much from him about entertainment law and life!

analysis.name: Jeannie IM
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She gives you a decent amount of work but she is a nice teacher and it is fairly easy to get an A. I revised one of my drafts in like 30 minutes and she gave me a 92. You will have to read out loud and talk to others tho.

It sucks that you have  an assignmentdue  every class; however,  that is not Jeannie's fault. She's a great teacher and has helped my writing improved. She's not rude, more like sarcastic. People have forgotten to turn in assignments and she'll still grade it. She's intimidating but you'll learn alot talking to her. She also brings treats!

Tough grader, but amazing professor. She really cares about you and has good exercises to improve. Attendence is mandatory, but if you're actually sick and usually go to class she'll let some stuff slide.

She is one of the best professors I've had so far. She is helpful both in and out of class. She often holds office hours to talk about essays. She offered extra credits twice last semester, which is very important in a writing class. She also offered letters of recommendation to the entire class at the end of the semester.

Great Professor, she was very kind. There will be a lot of group discussions, but most discussion topics are very interesting. If you tell her any concerns with your essay during your meetings, she will help you tremendously. Like every writing class, be prepared to read. She gives enough time for assignments. She has the best style of clothes!

analysis.name: Irina Langer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Niceish person, bad prof. Very disorganized, late to nearly every class and office hours/meetings. Grading feels arbitrary; taking her direct feedback doesn't improve grades on assignments. Assignments are posted late and in random places. Heavy reading load at times, but most of class is just watching movies. Long grading times. I learned nothing.

Prof. Langer's course stands out as one of the most fulfilling and engaging parts of my first sem. Despite other reviews, she created a safe and encouraging space where I felt comfortable sharing my opinion. She was easily accessible and patient when working with students. I never witnessed her 'shaming' anyone, so be mindful of online reviews.

Prof. Langer is very easy-going and a fun person to get to know. The class itself isn't too difficult and feels fairly casual rather than strictly academic. 
I enjoyed that we watched many films throughout the semester. Professor Langer also offers many opportunities for extra credit.
Overall, this class is a great option for a relaxing course.

Professor Langer is very educated on books, paintings, and movies. When it comes to discussions, she loves for students to be engaged. Her writing prompts will get you thinking about things you hadn't considered. She's a very nice and understanding professor. There are a couple of readings and movies, and you might need to purchase books.

Very disorganized and not that open minded to personal opinions in class. It's also difficult to meet her outside of class hours, and she will send readings to do before class very last minute. Shes kind but the course overall didn't feel stable and consistent with the syllabus.

analysis.name: Ida Chavoshan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Totally the best professor I've ever met. The course is easy, you only have to finish one essay during the semester. A few readings after class. She is kind, caring, giving feedback patiently. You can talk to her without any pressure.
Genuinely the best prof at NYU. I took her for writing as exploration. She really cares about students, fair grader, clear rubrics, lots of time to complete assignments.

Prof. Chavoshan was so inspirational and taught me so many important things during Bridgerton. She is nuanced, she is aware and she is interested in learning with her students. She has never talked at us and rather beckons us to add to what we already know. She is fantastic at giving feedback and has made me a more aware person.

Took her for WRCI over the summer and she was great! lectures kept me engaged and easy A. Midterm/final is one paper and she gives feedback during the step-by-step process. Had some breakout room talks but nothing too serious. We had weekly posts based on the articles we read-prompts are very clear! highly recommend taking her!!!

I took her online for WRCI, and she organized the course very well. She made her lectures as engaging as they could be online and was very clear with her class expectations. Most of the grade was one big project, which she gives good feedback on step by step, and the rest includes attendance, discussion posts, and a small presentation.

analysis.name: Irving Schenkler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Goofy dude who is a bit too into the class material given that it's common sense, but success is heavily based off of participation and the passion you show for the class. Grade is group-dependent but you individually control ~60% of final grade so just try to yap and smile and all will be well. Always go to feedback meetings after presentations

Prof Schenkler is the goat.

All you have to do in order to get an A is to participate once every discussion and do well on the 3 essays. He will give out 100% to everyone that follows his criteria (which he states multiple times in class). 

Ended the class with 100% on everything, while not reading any of the material.

The greatest C&C professor of all time. My only regret is not being able to take him for B&S. Participation matters heavily, but he is generous with grades and the class is fun. While other kids were busy reading 2000-word books, my class was watching great movies and having nice discussions.
Adorable, funny, intelligent! I am constantly impressed by his technology skills.

What a guy. Hands down one of the best writing professors at Stern. Classes are engaging and organized in a great way. Understands we are busy and doesn't expect us to read everything on the syllabus. Gives weekly journals with great feedback and the essays (although tedious to write) are pretty easy to score well just follow the rubric. 10/10!!!!!

analysis.name: Panos Ipeirotis
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: great guy, funny greek accent, and interesting class. he is enthusiastic about the material, but the class is so broad that we never get deep into the material. interesting group projects, boring individual assignments

Great guy, especially if you get him warmed up in his office. He is extremely passionate for his work, and if he feels that you are interested in learning the topic in depth he can spend a lot of time with you.
Nice guy, really passionate for what he is teaching. I wish all my other professors were as engaging as Panos
Panos is a great teacher. He really knows what he is talking about and he makes every effort to be available to the students. I enjoyed the class, even though I was not interested in the topic.

Loved his teaching, also could use ChatGPT on the final which was clutch. I think it really depends on your TA because she was the one who graded all my assignments. He's very approachable after class and as long as you put your face in his brain, he will grade well.

analysis.name: Isra Ali
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 110 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: When you take her tests, you can literally feel your gpa drop. Would not even recommend her to Satan.

Quoted saying she rather be "feared than loved" as a teacher. Assignments are frivolous yet time consuming, and her first mid-term was 60 multiple choice questions on specific talking points in her lecture - not the broader concepts we explore in recitation. Do not recommend.

assignments are short and easy but the class is impossible to follow. the smallest phrases or comments she makes in lecture are expected to be memorized and appear on tests. grading is unclear and even when everyone in a 200 person lecture gets a C, she will blame it on us not paying attention.
Her tests do not reflect the what the class is supposed to be about. She says she cares more about major concepts and not specific people and dates. You have to know everything. Not exactly fair.

Do NOT Prof. Ali if you can help it. She treats a 20-person seminar like it's an auditorium lecture: she talks nonstop, and even when she does engage with students, she does it by fishing for the answers she thinks are right. Tough grader, and vague about expectations. Her criticism is condescending and usually opinion-based, not constructive.

analysis.name: Irvin Ibarguen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Fantastic all around professor. His lectures are very useful and interesting, he's easy to reach outside of class for feedback, and although the course uses a textbook it's (intentionally) free and online. It's also pretty light reading every week, at least compared to most other history courses! Grading was clear, concise, and very fair.
He's the best. Such an easy class. Everyone walked out with an A. Take him if you can.

An extremely kind and caring professor! This class had a lot of reading (like 100-150 pages a week), but that's expected with an advanced history seminar. Gave us two free unexcused absences for the semester and was understanding when I needed an extension for a paper. 10/10 would take again!

A really sweet professor who cares a lot about his students and makes sure they understand the material. He made the workload extremely manageable because of the online format and the graduate student strike and was super accessible outside of class. He had really detailed and interesting recorded lectures and a Q and A every week. Highly recommend

Irvin was super accessible outside of class and really adapted well to the online format. The class is not really a lot of work, but it is very important to be diligent and stay up to date on lectures. As long as you do not slack you will do well in the class. Irvin is also super knowledgeable, and his lectures are some of the best I have ever seen

analysis.name: Kyle Jung
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ignore all the other review, Jung is the GOAT. Boy oh boy where do I start. Every class, a smile comes on my face. He brings joy to my day and is the only 11am class I would ever wake up for (I typically wake up at 2pm).  Although our class average on the midterm was a 63, he is still the GOAT for the W curve. I love you Professor Jung

He is very kind and has a sarcastic sense of humor (that apparently everyone takes seriously). The subject is difficult, for me at least, but he is very understanding. I recommend going to office hours where it's a lot easier to clear up any misconceptions, and he was especially helpful after the first midterm.

This guy is not it; pick literally anyone else. He's lowkey just a yapper. If you have a hard-to-pronounce name, beware. He won't call on you for participation. Hates actually having to host office hours and review sessions (sad that he "misses out on lunch"). Not as funny as he thinks he is.
Nice dude, doesn't budge on his rules no matter what. Tests way harder than all the practice/hws, Class test average was a 62.5. Make sure to lock in on time management or else you'll get cooked.
utilizes peak word salad during lecture, nothing from lecture/practice exam actually ends up on the real exams. run fast kids

analysis.name: Jennifer Jacquet
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Marine Ecology & Conservation. Immensely knowledgeable about the subject. Caring & approachable. Grading isn't too tough. Quizzes before every class (easy), four short papers, and a book review. Workload was lightened due to COVID & general stress, normally has a midterm & final. Still a lil strict about extensions. She's great, would take again!

Jennifer was clearly passionate about the class and I enjoyed the subjects covered in the class. However, she is very unaccommodating. My laptop broke right before an essay was due to the point where I had to ship it somewhere to get it fixed. She did not allow me an extension when I asked, and I know other students had similar issues with her

I still reference ideas from this class today! Jacquet is obviously very passionate about the material and is a super kind person. Her tests covered more material than expected, so take detailed notes in class. Do the readings (they aren't long but the parts she mentions in class will be on the test), take good notes, and you should be fine.

Interesting subject but professor made me hate the course. Don't take unless you are an environmental sci major or else you will feel lost and she won't care or help you. Also loves to shame, wrote a whole book on it. Doesn't give you feedback on what you got points off for. Overall a horribly frustrating experience with this prof

analysis.name: Jiri Motejlek
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Literally no idea how to teach...assignments were ridiculosuly long with no clear due date. Although the class isn't the most challenging, you're basically teaching yourself.
He does not know how to teach properly and the exams are testes on stuff not mentioned in class ever before. Don't take him no matter what.

analysis.name: John Scianimanico
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Support outside of class was minimal, and establishing any real rapport was extremely difficult. I wouldn't feel comfortable depending on this professor for mentorship or a letter of recommendation. By the end of the term, most students were simply glad it had ended. If possible, I strongly suggest selecting a different instructor for this course.

The class is challenging, and the teaching could be clearer. Lectures don't always explain the concepts in an easy-to-understand way, and the examples sometimes don't align well with the homework. The homework itself is difficult, and grading tends to be strict. Exams are also often harder than the practice problems provided.

This guy made my econ experience at NYU worthwhile. Patient, answered all my emails, and showed me grace when my mom was ill. He also wrote me a letter of rec for law school. Can't say enough good things about working with him, and during our last class, all of us thanked him for a wonderful experience. If you have to take this class, go with him.

This is the best econ prof at NYU. Prof. Scianimanico uses guided notes in each lecture to make sure you have all the information you need to succeed. He is very accessible outside of class and even outside of his office hours. Although most of your grade is exams, he explains everything that is going to be on the midterm/final before you take it.

Tough class but great teacher! Teaching style uses lots of examples and helps work out problems with us in class. Homework is difficult, but always available for office hours and recitation practices with a very similar problem set. Homework is graded very easily and tests are very similar in difficulty to homework.

analysis.name: Jinyang LI
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A lot of self study is required. Labs are difficult and grading is tough.

deadlines for labs are too tight. how do you teach pointer basics on wednesday and expect students to complete a 7 part lab culminating with an implementation of a binary search tree by Sunday? Huge disconnect between what she teaches and what she expects you to know.

Her lectures have too much insignificant fluff and we hardly get to the important details. Recitation provides little to no help, and is disorganized (most students skip). Labs are very hard & nothing like what's taught in lectures, and you pretty much have to teach yourself everything. Google is basically your professor. Avoid at all costs.

You will learn a lot. Very high workload. Labs are tough. Tests average around 50/100. Grading can be ridiculous. People receive 0s on labs because they incorrectly submit the grace days file format (i.e. submitting 4.25 instead of 4.5). Learned a lot, but unnecessarily/annoyingly strict and difficult for anyone not obsessed with C / CSO.
The labs are very difficult. The lectures have nothing to do with the labs. You have to learn a ton of things by yourself.

analysis.name: James Polchin
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Although Professor Polchin is somewhat of a tough grader, his class sets you up for success in the sense that there are two papers that you work on throughout the semester. This class did not cause me stress because he gives you so much time to work on your drafts, which I really appreciate. I would absolutely recommend you take him!!

only two essays but is a harsh grader. wants it to be journalistic but if it's not what he wants then you get a B. Both essays are on photography so it is difficult if you have zero interest or background in the subject.

Coming back to rate him. he is such a harsh grader and no worth taking. he made suggestions during office hours and when i put them he wrote that he didnt like it. super annoying and just not worth to take.

I do not understand all the negative reviews; Professor Polchin was great! His class is seminar-style, allowing you to connect with him and your classmates. He assigns two papers, a few short writing assignments, and, occasionally, has you peer review your classmates' writing. He makes the road towards the final draft very smooth. Take him!

Super light work outside of the actual class. In class just make sure you participate and your grade will be fine. Polchin is an awesome dude, and the stuff he teaches is pretty valuable. Easy grader too.

analysis.name: Kelli Moore
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I graduated from NYU a few years ago, and Professor Moore's class is the only one I think about years later. I learned so much in the time I spent in her classroom, and I cannot recommend her enough. It is a privilege to be one of her students. Grading is admittedly tough, but it's so worth it.

Prof Moore is a very intelligent professor and challenges students to think outside the box. The grading is not ideal as it is based off two papers that range from 5-10+ pages and are assigned DAYS in advance. Ambiguous preparation for tests and unclear grading. Race + Media was insightful but I wouldn't take it again for the sake of my GPA.

I took this class in the Spring 2023 semester and returned to write this review now because I haven't stopped thinking about it. Out of every class I took at NYU, this was by far the best. It opened me up to a new level of thinking, and I will always recommend it. I will remember Prof. Moore for her intelligence and kindness -- sign up if you can!

yes. yes. and yes. Take race and media with prof. Moore. Her lectures are both informational and entertaining. Though the class is reading heavy, the readings are incredibly interesting. For the final paper you can write about anything related to race and media so there's many options for you to express yourself creatively.

Professor Moore is an amazing lecturer and super sweet person. My only complaint is that the entire class was graded on two assignments (a midterm and a 10+ page final essay), and depending on who the TA is, the grading can be kind of tough. Interesting class but not sure I would take it again tbh.

analysis.name: John Sexton
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is for John Sexton's Relationship Between Religion and Government course. Most rewarding class I've ever had the privilege to take. Such heavy material made so interesting through Sexton's personal experiences. A must-take class if you have the chance. Don't miss out! Life-changing course.

John is seriously the best person I have ever met. This class is interesting whether or not you were interested in it before. It was a lot of reading, but it was worth it! Having a class with John is one of those once in a lifetime type of things - you really don't want to miss the chance.

John is an incredible teacher. He is born to teach. You learn so much from his intellect, experience and lectures but most importantly from his personality. He is a uniquely humble individual who values each person and relationship greatly. So lucky to have sat in his class for a year.

J Sex is amazing!  He genuinely cares about all his students and knows everything on the topic since he has so much first hand experience.  Everyone here should take a class with him or at least try to get to know him!

One of the hardest but most rewarding classes I've ever taken. Do not take his classes if you are not prepared for the workload, but best professor/teacher I have ever had. Kind, extremely smart, and truly cares about his students.

analysis.name: Karen Ralph
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ralph, very knowledgeable about Art History, is a difficult professor to work with. I thought it would be a great introduction, not nearly as writing heavy as it was. With that many written assignments, instructions could have at least been clear, (never the case). When trying to discuss the mixup she was dismissive and rude. Had to withdraw.

Karen... You love her or hate her or both. She is insanely knowledgeable, basically a walking encyclopedia. She can sometimes be hilarious, when it has to do with art. But in class, her priority is Gothic art, and if you don't do your reading or follow her mega-detailed rubric, she/you won't be happy. She can come off really cold, but learn a lot.

Professor Ralph was one of the most knowledgeable professors I've ever had. You could ask her any question and she would give you a thoughtful and incredibly detailed answer. Though she is a tough grader, if you put in the work you will get a good grade. Highly recommend taking her course at NYU Paris!

She genuinely doesnt care about her students. Never met a professor like her (and i mean that in the worst way.). Has a very strict grading rubric and only cares that you follow it specifically, doesnt care about your actual skill level. Gives you 10 minutes when you ask to meet with her.

Dr. Ralph is one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. She knows a crazy amount about medieval art/architecture/life (+ way more) and is eager to share this information, making the class engaging and informative. There is a decent amount of reading but it's not too hard as it relates to the subjects discussed in lecture. Take this class!

analysis.name: Azeta Kola
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: At least this year she's an easy A- grader, not an easy A. You don't really need to participate that much, but she did cold calls. Easy to reach out after class, but the grading criteria were really confusing. Never comment clearly on all the writings. Really cares more about Chicago style than what you wrote. don't take her if u are international

Shes kind of odd, but her class is really easy. She cold calls randomly so beware of that, especially if you are Chinese, because she loved cold calling us. Other than that, I never read anything for her class and still made an A.

Okay here's the thing, very sweet lady and clearly passionate. She's an expert in her field. However, this will be the most boring hour and fifteen minutes of your life. Her exams are exactly the study guide, and she's pretty easy going on the papers. I actually feel super bad bc sometimes it feels like she's talking to herself it's so boring.

Had a hard time trying to get an A in her class, grading criteria isn't clear. Class is easy because the lectures are just her speaking. Take this class with her if there are no other good professors left.

SUPER easy - she WILL give you A's on assignments if you try. She's very kind. However, it is truly the most boring class you will ever take. She drones on for 90 minutes (always goes over time), and her lectures are abominably dull. You can get by with just the summary of each reading. easy A, but less will to live. I fell asleep every time.

analysis.name: Kimberly Bernhardt
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Firstly, this is not a personal opinion, I am speaking for my whole class: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She cared about her ability to keep her job so she would pretend that she was helping you but she did not care about her students whatsoever. She offered office hours but they were useless along with her irrelevant feedback. I repeat, DO NOT CHOOSE HER

Smart person, terrible Professor. Constantly says irrelevant things during class, making her lectures very unproductive. Feedback is unclear and picky as hell. Grades really strictly.  For those who are still hesitating about whether to choose her, there must be better options.  For those who end up in her session, just Git Gud, life goes on.

Never have I met a more awkward teacher. She constantly stumbles over her words and makes concepts difficult to understand and argues with you if you have an opinion. The common expression "There are no wrong answers" does not exist in her classes as your answers are always met with uncertainty and an awkward laugh. Also, she gives too much HW.

Very tough grader. She fails at explaining herself, as well as what she expects from her student. Sometimes she would give you confusing or even opposite suggestions. It takes way too much time for a writing class like this. This professor even makes you take the course evaluation in front of her. Her class is always picked last. Think carefully!

She's is very picky and gives awful feedback. Constantly contradicts and says useless things. Participation is a must and don't even think about taking your phone out for a second. Very unclear about what is needed to be done for classwork/homework/papers. There are better professors out there but if you're stuck with her just suck it up and GL.

analysis.name: Nikolay Kukushkin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: worst professor ive ever taken at nyu. im a science major and very much so used to taking hard science classes, his "version" of science does not make any sense. ive never seen someone take a straight forward science and make it not make any sense- goes to show that credentials mean nothing

If what you value in a professor is fairness, clarity, and basic respect, I would not recommend taking his class. My experience was stressful, confusing, and handled with a level of carelessness that no student should have to deal with. Don't take him. Save your youth and energy for professors who actually care.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS! He does not share presentations or any notes before or after lectures - even though the information is useless for his exams. He doesn't even allow computers/iPads in class. His feedback was unnecessarily harsh and unreasonable. Students are randomly accused of plagiarism and the use of AI constantly even without any evidence.

got straight As on all personal quizzes, exams, and assignments, had a group essay where no one in my group did the work, and they all agreed on an idea that didn't apply to the assignment, when I emailed him he basically replied "do all the work yourself then" and refused to let us change the topic even though he himself knew it didn't apply.

honestly, this class was so hard for no reason. he is clearly very intelligent, and knowledgable in his subject. HOWEVER, the midterm and final exam are 80 true of false questions and 3 short answers. He is also a diva at times.

analysis.name: Karl Storchmann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 172 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Funny guy, lectures are pretty entertaining but oftentimes go off topic, usually about his love for drinking wine. Problem sets assigned infrequently, only around 6 per semester. 2 exams, both moderately hard. Main issue is class feels disorganized and hard to know how to study properly for exams.

I've been trying to figure out why I am attending the lectures. His lectures are indeed funny, yet while others laugh, I just hope he can go back to the topics that we should be discussing. This class is titled URBAN ECON, however, I fell like I am taking STUDIES OF WALAWALA and WINE IS BENEFICIAL classes at the same time. I am being really fair.

He deviates from the topic TOO MUCH. Not only he casually digresses, but he also talks about TOTALLY IRRELEVANT stuff from the course, such as wine, beer, or whatever drew his recent attention. So his class is easy. But the test itself - not so easy. And no practice exam! Some of his problems are not even from the lecture or from the problem set!

He is kind, patient and supportive outside of the class and he's very passionate about what he taught. Not that hard for a Econ 200. You can skip lectures and just study the notes. But it's not secure cuz he would test stuff that he only mentioned in class. The curve is insane cuz everyone cooked at the final. Will get a good grade if you studied!

no-BS answer:

lectures are boring. i barely went to them and the ones I did go I was on my phone. For tests, I studied the psets and quizzes (only took me 4 days to study for each midterm and final).

Very nice professor. Final exam median was under-70%, which suprised me b/c material is very starightforward and I got an A without going to class.

analysis.name: Larry Maloney
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a very nice man, but would not repeat. independent reading is a must, content not fully covered/confusingly articulated in lecture. Heavy reliance on AI. recitation had helpful slides I learned more there than lecture. going to class or recitation not as helpful though as independent study from the textbook.

Take any other class for your psych requirements -- prof is dry, unengaging, and often confused about what is going on. Grade is entirely based on 4 exams which sounds easy in theory, but some of the content wasn't even taught in lecture. Class deflated my GPA and stressed me out -- avoid avoid avoid!

4 tests make up ur entire grade, but he cancelled exam 3 despite the class avg being a 67%. Slides are mostly pictures, so even if u go to class, if u don't read the book you'll prob fail. BUT even if u do read the book, you'll prob fail anyway bc its unclear whats gonna be on the test. TA's were awful too, super rude + only read off their slides

Oh don't get me started on this man. I tried liking him, but no. He is so unclear, no communication, never responds to email and over all so unhelpful. The grading is so unfair. Like it deflates ur grade unless ur in the top 20%. I'm also disappointed in how things turned out because I genuinely did like the subject, but Proff's actions ruined it.

Overall it's an okay class. The exams r always so random, sometimes abt class content, sometimes abt textbook, or sometimes graphs. They are so confusing and unrelated that I feel like he isn't making those exams himself, but the recitation leaders r. After reading hundred pages I feel disappointed at the confusing Qs and students cheating behind.

analysis.name: Luis Ramos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: don't be scared of his syllabus - it looks tough, but he made all the exams take-home. Above all, genuinely learned a lot in this class and thoroughly enjoyed all the class discussions!

The GOAT. He tries to scare you during the first class (+ has a no devices requirement), but he's an incredibly chill prof. His readings were actually pretty interesting too. He made both the midterms take home, and is overall such a kind person
Literally the GOAT. Must take his class

Professor Ramos is amazing! Took him for both CFI and II. He seems really tough and intimidating at first, but after a couple lessons you'll soon see that he's so caring and such a lovely person. He is incredibly passionate about what he teaches and enjoys stimulating class discussions, so be sure to participate and get involved! Love Ramos!

At first, he seems very intimidating. Then, he backs down. If you participate, you will most likely get at least a B+. Two long midterms, and a group project. Must do readings because there are weekly quizzes.

analysis.name: Dimitri Landa
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I am currently sitting in this class, bored out of my mind and frustrated. I entered NYU wanting to be a political science major, but because of this class, I am changing my major. There are a lot of boring readings, there are impossible pop-quizzes, and the lectures would put anyone to sleep. Save your soul and do not take this class.

He's so boring and he assigns papers on a Friday and makes them due on a Monday. He must assume that NYU students spend their weekends twiddling their fingers, while the reality is that many students need weekends to work jobs to afford living at NYU, and preventing us from working on the papers on weekdays while working isn't fair.

Dimitri Landa is genuinely one of most EMBARASSING Professors in existence. 
I don't care how many fancy words he uses, he simply does not know how to get to the POINT. 
Additionally, he seems to enjoy punishing students that perform well on assessments, because he curved us down. 
Do not take this guy, he's PATHETIC!

The biggest complaint I have about him is how condescending he can be. I went to office hours to clarify my understanding (the text is very dense) and he was incredibly rude throughout the session. Rather than actually explaining the content, he spent the entire time belittling me.

Terribly boring. Prepare to fall asleep in lecture. The no tech policy is annoying. There are weekly quizzes during recitation- not too hard. Rob was my TA and he was truly the only good part about this class. Class material itself is not difficult.

analysis.name: Laine Nooney
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class single-handedly drained my soul and made me question several of my life choices. A large portion of the lectures is basically them reminding us that we are in a Top 10 school. They don't know how to teach properly, but they sure know how to grade harshly.

Extremely difficult to do well on the tests. They are graded very harshly. They don't know what they are expecting from us. If you want to cry over the course material before your test, then take this class. Otherwise run!!!!
Please, please, please avoid taking this class if you don't have to. I cry a little every time I enter that lecture room. MCC kids who have to take this course, godspeed.
I literally cant even stress this enough. Do everything in your power not to take their classes. Genuinely have never hated my life more. Like I'm so serious

While I appreciate how self-aware and approachable Prof. Nooney makes themself seem, the casualness of their teaching style makes their lectures wordy and quite hard to follow. They also expect a high level of specificity in our exams - which is difficult given how in-concise their lectures are. I'd avoid if possible

analysis.name: Lawrence Reed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 134 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: 3 exams with no drops, so you need to ace every exam to get an A in the class. Tests are easy if you memorize literally every single slide. You also don't have to show up to lecture since he records all of them. But make sure to watch them because he throws in bonus questions. Start studying 3 or 4 days before the exam and you should be golden!

Ian is an alright professor. Not the most respectful to women, not the most accurate about scientific evidence/interpretation. His lectures are engaging, but he isn't the best at facilitating discussions. When answering questions, seems like he's more concerned with proving that he knows what he's talking about than actually answering the question.

I wasn't a huge fan of the class. I understand that everyone is entitled to their own opinions, but as a professor teaching potential clinical psychologists, I think that he taught the class a lot of his own (sometimes inappropriate) opinions as if they were objective facts. For the tests make sure you can memorize information but it's manageable.

LOVEDDD abnormal psych, just attend lectures and memorize the highlighted info on slides, and you'll get an A. Don't listen to these other reviews, they didn't go to class. Extra credit was easy if you ATTENDED CLASS.

I'm not even sure what my grade in this class is and depending on one take home quiz (25%) I could drop from an A. I don't understand how the take home has so much weight vs the A average I have from all my exams. This class was unnecessarily hard for the class that it is. Professor also voices his "controversial" opinions as facts. Avoid.

analysis.name: Luke Trusso
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Can't love him more, one of my favorite profs so far. Wasn't a fan of LS courses but he enlightened my LS interests and you can always find his words inspirational to your life. I am seriously jealous of anyone who gets a chance to take his classes including me in 2025 so if you do please pay attention and you won't regret. Wish him all the best!

Prof. Trusso is awesome. Very caring, funny guy. Lectures and readings are very engaging, if you choose. Essentially no workload except 3 short essays w/ interesting prompts and super easy grading. Worst part of his class is being sad when 3/4 of the class never pays any attention to his great lectures. One of the GOATS. Take him!

This professor was by far the best I have ever had. His lectures were never boring, and everything he said was always super interesting. He is extremely knowledgeable in the topics he teaches and very hilarious too. TAKE HIM if you get the chance, you will not regret it. If I could take the class with him again I absolutely would.

so i love luke. he is witty and funny and sarcastic and an absolutely wonderful teacher. the class is so engaging and he teaches the material in such an absorbing way- i don't even need to take notes. he is just lovely.

The indisputable GOAT. Lectures are never boring. Zero homework/prep needed because he goes over everything in class anyway. Really encourages discussion, and offers unique perspective on readings. 

And the best part... he hands out A's like candies. You'd really have to try to get anything other than an A, I'm serious.

analysis.name: Marian Thorpe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor, very knowledgable and kind professor. The class includes 2 short 750 word in-class essays that you know the prompt before and can prepare what you need to write. 2 essays. And 1 in-class final essay (you also know the prompt before). Grading is very clear and it is very easy to get an A

PSA: There is a lot of writing in this class, with three in-class exams and two essays. The course can also feel repetitive as every class revolves around small group discussions. However, Prof Thorpe is extremely kind, knowledgeable, and understanding with her students. She grades fairly and is always open to chat. I recommend taking her class!

Dont be fooled by the old ratings. New syllabus now. 3 tests and 1 paper. Work is manageable but unnecessary - she will assign 4 hr long movies/readings per week. Most of class is discussion, but frankly, most students arent knowledgeable enough to provide anything too insightful. Barely teaches. If you want to use your time wisely, dont take her.

Too many essays for one class: 2 in-class essays for midterms + 1 media analysis essay + 1 long paper + 1 in-class essay for final. Before every class, we have to read articles or books/watch movies/do pre-lecture quizzes, not hard but unnecessary work. Don't take her if you want an easy A to fulfill college requirements.

It is very clear that Prof Thorpe cares about the well-being of her students. She is amazing at giving constructive feedback that helps students succeed. She is one of the sweetest people I have met at NYU and just seems like one of those people you can have a nice conversation with. She never stops smiling and radiates positivity. TAKE HER!!!!!!!

analysis.name: Michael Walfish
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: For the love of your life, please avoid. The only good thing about his class are his explanations. Other than that, this class is hell. The workload is super intense. I barely had time for other classes. Furthermore, he is such a tough grader.   Briefly, this class is so annoying and hard that I had to consider counseling after finishing it.

Extremely poor at teaching. His notes didn't go into details at all and besides the notes, all materials on operating system he provided is the textbook, which was long, vague, boring and not helpful. And he even said that some of what textbooks said was wrong. So why didn't he prepare his own materials? He didn't want to help students at all.

Hardest class I've taken at NYU. The tests were incredibly difficult and he expects you to have a deep understanding of every single concept.

He's incredibly smart and a good professor (though probably overqualified), but sometimes overcomplicates things to flaunt that he's smart.

Prayers to anyone who has to do lab4 in the future
RUN! Take anyone but don't him.

Walfish is very articulate and knows the material  well. He does an excellent job verbally explaining the content. Having said that, the class is incredibly difficult. The amount of homework and labs is unreal, even excessive. The exams require super detailed knowledge. Very hard class.

analysis.name: Matthew Santirocco
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Love Matthew! You'll need to read to understand what's going on, and he'll put you in groups to work on an assignment every week. (he talks a lot, so every other week if you aren't 1 or 2) The essays are a little hard, but if you take his feedback to heart, you'll improve. You do have two trips to museums that I thought were not necessary.

The seminar class was online the whole semester which was not good for discussions. He went over the books we read really quickly. You are required to go to 2 museum trips during the semester on a Sunday which didn't even help much with the class material and was a waste of time. Take a different seminar class if you can.

Prof. Santirocco is well respected in his field and incredibly knowledgeable about Classics, it's a privilege to take a class taught by him. He is very passionate about academia and expects students to take his class and their work seriously. So don't take his class if you're insouciant about school or a slacker.

Prof Santirocco is truly an amazing professor. He cares a lot for every student and accommodates to them, even if he has to take time out of his own schedule to do so. LOTS of reading (about 130 pages per week) and you need to speak in class. Tests and essays are fair. I highly recommend taking him if you have the chance.

Prof Santirocco is one of the best professors I have ever had. I have taken two Advanced Latin courses with him and always looked forward to each class. He is very knowledgeable, but he is in no way condescending and is always eager to consider everyone's opinions. He cares deeply about the subject and his students. It's hard work, but worth it!

analysis.name: Nancy Xenakis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Xenakis is knowledgeable, but the class is mentally draining. She lectures for hours without meaningful breaks. Despite appearance she actually  has little consideration for students. Concerns about a 2-hour placement were dismissed with no support. I felt discouraged, not guided, and dismissed. Would not recommend.

As a first-year MSW student on the two-year track, I enjoyed taking Practice I with Professor X. She is welcoming and approachable, with a strong work background in social work. Assignments are manageable, and she's always available to discuss. She's thorough with every task. The class prepared me well for my placement, and I highly recommend it!
I want to give her a 10 if I could

analysis.name: Andrew Needham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I love this class so much. The exams aren't hard if you study a fair amount and read. Amazing.

Such a fantastic professor! Graded on 4 essays and a 2500-word final paper. It is a bit of work, but his enthusiasm and cheerfulness make the class worth it. You must participate in the class to do well. Would recommend and willing to take againn

The professor is a nice enough guy, but the class is full of reading (300+ pages a week). The TAs run the class, and grading is ridiculous. Everyone gets a B on the midterm, and TA-professor continually screw students over. If you want to maintain a high GPA avoid this class at all costs. I dont even think the TAs could get an A the way they grade.

Professor Needham is phenomeal. I had him for Environmental History of NYC. The class consisted of in-depth lecture and field trips to environmental sites in NYC. Really unique way of teaching, yet he was able to connect with everyone in the class. Lenient grading, approachable, and open to different viewpoints on topics.

I LOVED Prof Needham!! Took him + Stephen Gross for C&C and they were both amazing. Lectures were very engaging and he loves cracking a good dad joke. Obviously cares a lot about the topic and his students and does his best to make every class interesting. Not too much reading outside of lecture and 3 short essays that make up the grade.

analysis.name: Paul Aarons Ngomo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor PAN is a very sweet and funny professor, however the class is not very engaging. As someone deeply passionate about philosophy, history, and cultures (especially within antiquity), I suprisingly dreaded attending this class. No tests, but mid-terms/finals are 3 5-8 page essays due within 7 days. Also, graded by AI but he's a fast grader.

biggest waste of time ever, but it's a required LS class so I guess you were wasting your life to begin with. prof uses chatgpt presentations, syllabus, and grading. the audacity is genuinely stupefying. content is extremely shallow, basic, and worthless. Since he teaches using the answers chatgpt gave him, you should just use chatgpt as well.

So. Much. Readings. For sure lecture heavy, he talks about interesting things from time to time. If you at least do spark notes of the readings you should be good for the lectures because he does explain majority of the key things in class. If I absolutely HAD to take him again I would. He is a very fair grader and gives great feedback I will say!

Professor Ngomo is the absolute goat. I wish I could take his class during the actual semester instead of during the summer. His lectures are heavy but the way in which he presents the information is so incredibly intriguing and helpful. I love the way he answers questions; very direct but informational at the same time. Love this guy :)

lectures give me a headache with the amount of questions he asks. lots of reading that no one completes, completing the readings will take you hours each night. however, he does give good feedback on papers. I honestly dread going to this class.

analysis.name: Nina Verneret
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Nina is a great teacher; she goes through the material at a good pace and makes sure to take time to help you understand if she can tell the class is struggling. Sometimes she will go really fast, though, then we work backward on a unit for a bit. Gives extra credit opportunities. She is heavy on pronunciation because she's from France
very nice and very communicative! assignments were fair and the chapter tests were exactly related to classwork and homework.

Prof. Verneret's class is the most fun I've had in my first year. She truely ensures a good vibe in her class, and the exams are really easy. Minimal workload. Though she doesn't seem to be very accessible outside of class.
AMAZING PROFESSOR DEFINITELY PICK HER FOR FRENCH! great lectures and grading is also so good you will fall in love with french!

She is super approachable and patient which makes learning French a lot less intimidating. Her lectures are fun with her own materials. Grading is fair and clear, gives useful feedbacks. She is NOT one of those profs who waltz into a classroom expecting everyone to know something about French even though it's an elementary class. Highly rec.

analysis.name: Roberta Newman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
most honest review of roberta newman:

she is great, currently taking her and i wish i could take her forever. yes she isnt tech savvy, could get off track sometimes, and loves to ramble, but she is just authentically her all the time and its apart of her charm 

super light grader, cares about her students and is passionate about everything.

I just would try to find someone else to take. She is very much not tech savvy as much as she claims to be. 25% of the class would just be waiting for her to set up and login to Brightspace. The readings were not that intriguing. 2 essays, one final project, a midterm, and a final. Be there for lectures or then the 
midterm/Final will be difficult.

I had a medical issue towards the beginning of the course and this is the one professor that was extremely caring. She truly cares about the success of her students and is looking to connect with them. One of the most wise people I've met and the lectures were so fun to listen to!

prof newman is sweet and funny! her grading criteria is clear and although she may ramble a lot in class, it makes the lectures actually bearable as it's not just an overload of info at once. the exams and projects are also pretty straightforward. take her!

KINDEST WOMAN EVER!!! She just wants students to care, so participate, act like you really know the material, and be friendly, and you will do amazing. Barely any graded work, all of which are very easy

analysis.name: Joseph Osmundson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Joe is very condescending and a much tougher grader than the other TAs. I did more work for this one credit POB lab than I did for POB itself. Avoid at all costs.

His social media presence is unprofessional, and his interactions in class often feel passive-aggressive and unnecessarily complicated. This makes him difficult to work with and creates an uncomfortable learning environment. I'm raising this because it's affecting the quality of the course.

Do yourself a favor and run.Writes in chicken scratch and talks unnecessarily fast. If you ask him a question, he'll just ask you right back. Makes things super hard to understand when this isn't even that hard of a class in the first place.

Restored my faith in Bio dept. He humanizes scientific learning and is truly passionate about the subject material (Protein Biochem). As long as you show up and pay attention you'll succeed on exams, which test for understanding not rote memorization. Lenient grader and helpful outside of class.

Do not take this professor. He makes a 1 credit class much harder than it should be, does not explain what he expects on assignments, and does not provide enough resources for homework and studying. Most of the students have no idea what is going on in this class.

analysis.name: Oded Regev
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: professor is attentive and responsive in OH and after class. Exams are 80% of the grade, but I think that is just how Algorithms classes are weighted. The exams are graded very harshly compared to the difficulty of the content on the exams, but I guess it doesn't matter in the end since there is a pretty large curve on the midterm and final each.
EXAMS ARE 80% OF GRADE AND NO SIMILAR TO HOMEWORK VERY VERY HARD CLASS
His lectures are amazing! Just be aware that two exams make up 80% of your grade.

Very clear lecture, excellent organization and easy to follow. The HW assigned beautifully complemented the lectures by giving the students a chance to not only practice the concepts discussed in lecture, but also to preview the next lecture's material in a very engaging manner: it guided students in thinking from the point of view of a researcher.

A truly amazing professor! Great lectures, very helpful in office hours, accessible on campuswire, clear explanations and fun demos... there's not much better you can get. The issue is the course is designed against you: two exams are most of your grade, not the weekly hw that takes hours, which is where most of the bulk of learning comes from.

analysis.name: Ola Galal
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't understand her at all. You can get C's on your papers, ask her for feedback which she won't give, then she'll give you an A at the end of the semester for all the pain and strife she caused. She gets super bugged about notification sounds during class so you can't have a phone or laptop during class. You also can't use the bathroom.

Extremely passive aggressive and restricting. Doesn't engage with student views much or encourage a lively classroom environment. No technology policy, no bathroom breaks, feels like a prison. Unnecessarily nitpicks every little thing done and tries to be tough and strict as possible. Class is disappointing& boring despite having so much potential

This is probably the worst professor I have ever taken during my academic career. She is extremely disorganized, can't follow her syllabus, and has difficulty remembering her words and rules. She wanted to be tough so bad that she did not give students a space to grow or be heard.. it gave identity crisis. Don't take this professor.

Don't take this lady. She is extremely passive aggressive and so strange. She won't let you have an opinion that differs from her's and she will not answer your questions if you need help. Hardly accessible outside of class (5 minute office hour appointments) and she grades papers randomly even if you do well on the HW. No bathroom during class too

This will be one of the easiest classes you will take. She is a super easy grader. You have 1-2 readings per class but you can get by by just skimming it. Each class, you basically get divided into groups and have to use the reading to answer questions.

analysis.name: Colm O'Shea
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Every minute I spent in his class or in one-on-one conferences, I felt like I was getting smarter. He really challenges you to think more deeply without assigning too much work. His vibe is very intense (we didn't introduce ourselves at the beginning of the semester because he wanted to learn how we think first), but he's really caring!

Super smart dude! I could listen to him talk for hours. He's strict in a way that inspires us not pressure us into exhaustion. Knows how to get our brains going, gives amazing feedback and knows exactly what to say. Sweet and funny! Honestly made me not hate writing essays!

One of the smartest people, let alone professors, I have ever met. He has such a passion for the work that he does that he makes me want to succeed. After one read through of my essay in a one on one conference and 20 minutes of discussion he was able to help me see my subject in a much clearer, and more interesting way. Simply, he's the bomb.

This class was so hard for me and really made me think, however I feel like I have a lot to take away. Colm is a really great professor, I was consistently shocked by how smart he is. He's a tough person to impress, but when you do impress him it's rewarding. No easy A, but you can get a lot out of his class.

Very good at giving you direction in your writing when you're confused about how to proceed. He often will take all the mismatched ideas I have in my head and give them a specific name that's a term I can research and this does wonders for my papers. He makes a very difficult task so much easier.

analysis.name: Olena Ciftci
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ciftci is a fantastic professor! I've taken two of her classes and had the best learning experience. Her grading is very clear and her door is always open for feedback and improvement. If you put in the effort, getting an A in her class is very doable. Her lectures teach you a lot, and she will always support you in and out of the classroom!

Professor Ciftci is one of the most incredible professors I have taken. She cares about her students SO much, inside and outside of the classroom. I would absolutely take her again. I loved walking in and seeing her smiling face welcoming us. She also gives a lot of help when needed. 10/10 professor.
lectures can be kind of boring but she is very nice

Lectures are not engaging and prof speaks monotone. I wouldn't avoid her at all costs, but definitely be mindful and don't be afraid of asking questions in class. More of a strict grader but she means well.

Honestly, the professor was so boring and harsh when it came to grading and participation. The topic of the class was already dull, and the class itself was not engaging. There wasn't much teaching; the professor simply read off slides, which means we could have stayed home and done it in our own time. I would not recommend this class

analysis.name: Omid Mehrgan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't trust what he says, no matter how he tries to reassure you. Just follow the syllabus and do the best you can — maybe you'll still pull off a good grade. But if you don't participate in class, there's no way you're getting a B+ or higher.
Finals and Essays were quite easy. However, we had group presentations that were harshly critiqued. Unclear grading, very arbitrary in a lot of ways. However, pretty easy to just float by.
Absolute joke of a “professor “ who cares more about comma pronouncing, sound rythms, and personal political opinions
Participation matters more than your essays. Very easy to do well but it is so boring.
If there are other options, never choose him

analysis.name: Si On Yoon
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor! Nice, inspirational, and accessible outside of class. You can always go to her office hours, and her TAs are nice too. This class is very test-heavy though; there is basically a one-page quiz every week or every other week, and there are two midterms and one final. You must review, review and review (if you want an A)!!!

SO interesting and ORGANIZED. Very clear expectations and and concise in her lessons. It's an exam-heavy class, but the questions were fair for the frequency of the exams. I didn't have to dedicate too much time outside of class. I went to lecture, recitation (mandatory), and studied for max 2-3 hours per week and got an A. Gives extra credit opps.

Professor Yoon is amazing and greatly cares about her students.  There are quizzes every week or so (they are not that difficult), along with 2 midterms and a final. The questions are mostly multiple choice, but there are also some short responses and true/false. There are also 3 extra credit opportunities. Her class is very interesting!

analysis.name: Sahar Parsa
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Parsa is a fantastic professor. She makes me see daisies and rainbows. She gives me a reason to live day in and day out. I hope one day I become half of the woman she is. After every lecture, I go to the top floor of my apt building, look down, and admire the beauty of the roads of New York before going back inside to begin a delightful R quiz

Prof Sahar is the best prof Ive ever seen. Her classes are great for us to practice self learning skills (cuz she teaches nothing and tests everything). In her amazing R exams, it is kind of her to leave us enjoy the beauty of those lovely codes by ourselves . I really appreciate her effortless efforts in letting me know the malice of this world.

It is an absolute disgrace for a school like NYU to hire such a professor to teach the most important course at the undergraduate level for Econ students. I have no idea where all the ratings above 1 came from. I give her a 1 simply because it is the lowest rating I can choose from not because she deserves it. Think twice before you take it.
She may be knowledgeable but definitely not good at teaching. Her video only provide the simple basis but you need to expect large amount of questions at test and very difficult. R.U.N if you could.

Econometrics is probably the most challenging class that I have taken at NYU. In order to be successful in this class, you will need to teach yourself everything, stay on top of ungraded homework, and go to OH. The exams were very silly because the TAs have different grading scales, so you could be screwed if the wrong one grades yours. Goodluck

analysis.name: Hesam Oveys
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 156 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I got him for MFE I and he is a very clear teacher. If it's not in the notes, it is unlikely to be on the exam. This makes it easy to study for his tests if you go to class, pay attention, and do the homework. Not very difficult if you try.

Hesam is my favorite math professor at NYU. He is organized and clear about his expectations. There is a lot of material but there are no surprises on his exams. Take this class if you want a direct teacher who is always happy to help you.

Hes an excellent teacher. I took him 4 MFE1&decided 2 take him for MFE2. Hes super clear&straight foward. He will always provide u with a basic explanation or a structured procedure as to how to approach a problem&then will dive into practice problems that start off easy&gradually get harder. If u understand everything in his lecture notes ur good

I took math for econ-1 and loved the course. His lectures are very good and he explains concepts very well. There is a lot of homework and there are 3 exams for this course but it isn't that difficult. If you got through the class notes, you should be in a good place for the exams.

Hesam Oveys is by far the best professor I have encountered at NYU so far. He takes great care in preparing his lectures and has clear guidelines for grading. He solves problems and explains concepts thoroughly in class and puts his notes online. His exams test only what he has taught and are quite easy. Worth taking.

analysis.name: Liming Pang
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Best Abstract Algebra lecturer at nyu. Introduces abstract ideas very well. The course itself is hard but the professor explains it so well that a novice (knowing a bit of set theory and general proof techniques) mathematician can understand.

Very kind and helpful professor outside of class. His lectures can be somewhat difficult to understand, and he does spend a lot of time on proofs, which are not tested. Grading system is fair, but the final was way harder than the 2 midterms.

Pang is a great lecturer for advanced math courses. He has a knack for explaining abstract concepts to make undergrad students understand by illustrations. Posts clear notes online. Homeworks are challenging, but they really help for doing well in the midterm and the final. He is also very patient during office hours. TAKE HIM IF POSSIBLE.

Professor Pang is amazing! Ive studied with him for two semesters and I highly recommend him! His lecture is well-organized and clear. He is pretty smart- he can relate the lecture topics to different math areas. He is extremely helpful, patient and hilarious. You can also expect anecdotes about famous mathematicians in his class : )

He is a very nice professor. I continued studying with him for two semesters and it turned out to be great! He is always patient, and after class, whenever I had question he was always willing to answer me. I learned a lot from him, and I am very appreciate of learning from him. Hope to meet you again!

analysis.name: Pablo Querubin Borrero
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's great. Very charismatic and truly just one of those people who's calling in life is teaching. He's smart and explains complicated concepts very well. Lectures are important, but the slides are posted online and are easy to follow on your own. 2 tests, 2 writing assignments. I got an A, just going to lecture and not doing any of the readings.

This professor is extremely caring and charismatic and a great, passionate educator. The class isn't very difficult at all but is very informative and useful for poli sci students interested in Latin American politics and the political economy. He explains complex concepts very well, has a good speaking pace, and adds really exciting anecdotes.

I had an amazing experience with Pablo this past semester. Truly a great teacher, who is somehow able to make theory and models interesting. Really opened my eyes to the complexities that exist when talking about Latin American politics. If you go to the lectures and pay attention you'll be fine.

One of the best professors I have ever had at NYU. Though there are a lot of readings, him and his lectures explain these concepts beautifully where you do not have to have a political nor economic background to understand. If you study his slides and pay attention in class you will get an A. Would 100% take his class again

Professor Querubín is an extremely knowledgeable guy and truly an expert in his field. His focus was more theory based and the application of these theories to case studies rather than more contemporary Latin American politics. However, the class is super easy and lectures can be quite interesting. You can get an A just by reading the slides!

analysis.name: Qi Lei
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Sometimes we learn to understand ourselves and understand others when we let go of our cravings and projections. In this term, Prof. Lei shifted my life to a certain degree.
I remember the night I observed the dark but peaceful ocean near the harbourside of Newport, sitting there to realize that life only flows. I hope she can enjoy a happy life.
Professor Lei is the most gentle, kind, and patient professor I have ever met. Also, she is very knowledgeable. The grading is really good.
The materials are hard, but the grading is quite lenient. I think for the midterms and finals i did a few problems wrong but Professor give me lots of scores. Take her if you want an A.
She is very patient and helpful, you can always get very detailed explaination during her office hour
