The professor frequently made errors when explaining proofs, which required students to spend extra time verifying. Additionally, the grading for the final exam lacked transparency, with no clear feedback or explanation provided.

analysis.name: Quang Vuong
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Had him for ECONUA18. His lectures are not the best as he just reads off powerpoints for 75 minutes. But he dos try to make this course as digestible as possible for students. Tips: show up to the lectures and consult the textbook (he doesn't like the textbook but exam questions are similar to textbook problems but more difficult of course).
Love this dude! Best teacher ever ever. Brilliant researcher, incredible teacher, an inspiration for us all! Highly recommend.

Firstly, his lectures are so lazy, for the first half of the semester his lectures were a projection of a pdf of the textbook where he would just read off exactly the textbook and just solve the already solved textbook problems. Then the TAs are choosing the HW problems while his exams are NOTHING related to class content.

analysis.name: Wang Qiuyu
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: In 603 and 604, students will complete a realistic corporate advertising task in the form of a group project, which is a valuable and engaging practical opportunity. The professor is not only kind and approachable but also deeply cares about her students—she replies to emails instantly and will go out of her way to help students.

Students from different cultural backgrounds fit well in this class, and a wide range of opinions is encouraged. Class participation and discussion are a major part of your grade. In general, students and the professor will share the talking time. If you rarely speak or do not like group discussion, your final grade will be affected.

The 603 course includes an interview project, two enterprise-related projects, and several guest speaker lectures. Most assignments are applied: you analyze real situations, prepare presentations, and reflect on what you learned. Overall, the work focuses on using course concepts in concrete projects rather than only taking tests.

Not an easy A, there will be solid workload. I took Cross Border Insight 603 and 604, these are not “light” classes. There is regular reading, writing, and project work. If you are looking for an easy 4 credits with minimal effort, these courses are probably not for you.

Wang Laoshi is great. She cares a lot about her students; you can email her outside class. I took her Cultural Insights of Business Communication course. She gave us many opportunities like bringing in the Yamibuy CEO and other guest speakers. The homework isn't bad but participation does matter. Show up and be ready to share your opinion!

analysis.name: Patrick Egan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Egan is by far one of the best professors in the politics department. I was hesitant in taking POL850 since I'm generally bad at math and coding but he did an amazing job of explaining concepts and did he not expect us to be experts in coding. The class is manageable, test heavy but it is open note. Take him, he loves his job and his field :)

Best professor in the poli sci department! Super interesting and informative lectures. The instructions and slides are clear and easy to understand. The wording on the exams can be a little ambiguous and confusing, and the grading is a bit strict, but as long as you understand the material, the exams should be easy.

Prof Egan is so wonderful. I truly knew nothing about anything statistics or computers but he broke things down so well. He really wants you to understand and will do anything he can to help. He is also so funny and kind! If you have POLUA850 as a major requirement and are super humanities-oriented do not be scared :)

content of class was boring and exams were tough but professor egan was genuinely really interested in us succeeding and he was so passionate about the subject which made the class more enjoyable. Explains everything very well and I would barely feel lost in his lectures.

tests are open note, only 3/5 homeworks are graded. attendance is not required but i suggest attending to catch the tips and tricks he gives during class. recitation attendance also isn't mandatory but for homework help it's great, tests are like the homeworks

analysis.name: Catherine Quan Damman
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The course is about LGBTQ and feminism. Professor Damman made it clear that this is not an easy A class. To get a decent grade requires prior knowledge in and alignment with leftist positions. She is enthusiastic, but the course structure is not as clear (going over one after another artwork and artist without a clear spine of logic).

Attendance is taken for every lecture & theres no textbook so you HAVE to go. Participate often. The class is lowkey just memorization of what your TA and professor says for each work. Be prepared to take lots of notes. Try to be remembered by your TA so you can get a good grade since the syllabus weighs the 3 papers & 2 exams, but no grade cutoffs

Be so wary. I got above a 93 on every exam, and a pretty good grade on every essay, and I still ended up with an A-. For some reason due to the absurd curving of this course, im pretty sure a 96-97 counts as an A-. For that reason, you could do everything almost perfectly in this course, receive minimal to no feedback, and still get points off.

professor quan damman is amazing. she is an incredible lecturer! easily on of the most engaging and interesting  professors at nyu. she cares about her students and is very compassionate and empathetic. there are not enough good things i can say about her.

analysis.name: Mark Ramos
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall, it is an easy class, and you can get to learn a lot if you take the initiative. A bunch of different majors in one class, so the course and teaching is not technical; he is more on the reading and project-heavy side. He really needs to get much more organized, and the demos are not helpful. You won't have any problems with grades.

roadmap to the course is very clearly stated in his syllabus. attendence isn't "taken" but there are in-class activities that count towards your attendance, which IS part of your final grade. his grading guidelines are clear in every assignment, and he's also very easy to talk to about the grades you receive. take him if u can!! super nice guy :)
Spent a lot of the class troubleshooting and the class felt disorganized and boring. Prof is nice, but all of the grading criterion is very vague. I think the subject (database) was just very boring.

If you are ever going to have to do anything website-related, TAKE THIS CLASS! He does an amazing job at teaching and formatting the class and it's a great intro to how to make a website from scratch. Easy A, if you do the work and the final project, is to make a website of your choice so it leaves you with something tangible.
He is sooo sweet. His powerpoints are concise, gives good lectures, and super clear w how to get a good grade. Take his class!

analysis.name: Jennifer Quilter
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Jenni is absolutely phenomenal!!! She deeply cares about her students and always asks how we're doing. Not only are the exercises she provides significant in aiding our final progression, but they're also very fun! Her feedback is so thoughtful and helps significantly. Please, whatever you do, TAKE THIS CLASS! You will have zero regrets!!!

I LOVE Jenni. She truly cares about her students, which is reflected in the students motivation / dedication to make her proud. Her class isn't easy, but it's worth it. She provides a safe / open environment, and I could say so much more, but long story short: She's amazing. Take her class. I absolutely loved being in her class, thank you Jenni!

You will truly find no other teacher as amazing as Jenni. She fosters an incredibly caring and supportive environment, and makes sure that we all get to know each other personally. Feedback is amazing and very clear. Homework is incredibly useful and helps with your final draft. Grading criteria is crystal clear, she makes sure we understand it.
Take her. You won't regret it. I'm not an Ai.

Jenni wants you to succeed, and you can feel it. You'll find yourself genuinely caring about an essay for the first time in your life. Although she sometimes lets the low-effort slackers slip by, if you're dedicated to writing, or at least want to be, Jenni can push you forward. Changed my writing forever. Thanks, Jenni.

analysis.name: Shengguo Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: yes he is nice and answers questions but is such a stickler for grading. i got points off on pre lab for my drawings being too small and for not drawing out the reference tables in the manual. seems like he just takes points off to avoid giving A's to everyone.

can be hard to understand at times because of his accent, but overall super nice; is willing to help with whatever and explains how to solve the postlab questions in a way that doesn't give away the answer; can seem a little cold at first, but is a good lab instructor!

i love this man so much he is genuinely so sweet and takes the time to walk you through procedures/questions if you don't know what to do or don't understand . it's clear he cares about his students and he's super passionate about what he does . best lab instructor ever

Professor Zhang is an amazing lab professor. He cares a lot for his students and wants everyone to do well. He is always willing to explain any procedural steps or chemistry concepts. He is also a nice grader. Highly recommend!
Don't understand the great views. Keeps on rushing me during lab and pressures me. Called other people smart when comparing them to me. Heavy accent too.

analysis.name: Michael Salgarolo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Note that all the grading is done by the TA, not the professor, so your ultimate experience is highly dependent on who your TA is. My TA, Weiyu Dang, was extremely smart and very knowledgeable (I'd say he is even more knowledgeable than the professor), but he was a very hard grader. Still, I learned a lot, and enjoyed the class.

The class definitely opened me up to concepts/ideas I hadn't learned before. It seemed like the class was critiquing colonialism and America through the lens of Asian history. The exams are straightforward and you are given all the content to prep for. The readings were not necessary except those for the essays. TA grades all the submitted work.

He is a truly abysmal professor who wastes students' time and tuition. Lectures add nothing, exams are needlessly harsh and misaligned; materials are posted late. He does not keep his word, stutters under basic questions, downgrades any work he cannot grasp and replaces teaching with ego driven theatrics. He should have stayed a worthless comedian.

He was a comedian before, so the lectures are occasionally funny. He stares at you if you whisper or take out your phone. Sometimes his voice is monotone and he stutters noticeably but he can't control that! TA grades everything so it's dependent on that. I had Weiyu and he was amazing. He forces you to actually grow which I appreciated.

Although I was a little scared to cover most of Asian history at once, he made it quite interesting and he made sure that students felt included by having small group discussions. His slides were very clear and organized for someone who takes notes on essential information. I did learn a LOT as an international student!

analysis.name: Ann Macy Roth
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Loves Egypt, but too much. Would rather hear her own voice than teach. Doesn't learn students names. Values her social life over class. Shows up late often. Takes months to grade papers that shouldn't take more than a week, two at most. Constantly changes due dates. Unorganized. Can't remember what she has/hasn't gone over.  Got tenure & gave up.

Took Cultures and Contexts. Knowledgeable on the subject, doesn't necessarily translate to her being an good or even adequate professor. Goes off on tangents/shows up late, not to mention that she takes an extreme amount of time to grade work. inconsistent grading. Got my course grade a month and a half after the semester ended. DO NOT TAKE
Professor Roth is overly interested in the subject and is unclear as to what information is relevant and what is just her going off on tangents. Incredibly boring and lots of work.

By far the WORST class I have ever taken. When grading essays, the professor and two instructors have completely different and subjective approaches leading to an incorrectly skewed grading curve of the class. Recitations were enjoyable but did not relate to lectures. Lectures were unorganized and incomprehensible. I HIGHLY regret taking this class

I didn't know that Art History could be boring, until I had this professor.  Completely unhelpful.  Unclear.  Late on returning emails, assignments, posting reviews.  She may just need some more teacher training...

analysis.name: Elayne Tobin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 82 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is my favorite professor. She is so funny, inspirational, cool, and hip. She goes off on tangents but her tangents are interesting too. She doesn't grade until the end of the semester so you won't know your grade till the end either. She doesn't assign a lot of homework and we don't have that many papers either. TAKE HER, YOU WON'T REGRET IT!

She is an amazing prof, allows students to be creative with their assignments and basically choose what they want to write about. If you make the time to go to her office hours she is extremely helpful and will guide you in the right direction. I would recommend taking her! She really cares about her students.

Elayne is absolutely incredible and truly made my first semester at NYU.  Not only did she teach me so much about writing, but she helped me to get excited about my surroundings and to be curious. Absolutely brilliant and hysterical, really looked forward to every class. Readings and documentaries are fascinating as is she. TAKE HER.

She is such an interesting woman! She's so full of life and so hip! The readings were sometimes dry, but do them so you can contribute to class discussion. One tip: Sit at the front of the class because she mostly picks on the students in the front row to participate. She lets you do rewrites, but beware you won't know your grade till the very end

I don't even need to say anything, just TAKE her class!!!!!!!  Professor Tobin is the best; she is so caring, funny, and inspiring. Classes are super chill and we only needed to do two major assignments. She even invited us to eat Bareburgers after class like cmonnnnn take her and you won't regret it. GOATTTTT I love her so much

analysis.name: Peter Unger
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Although I remember absolutely nothing as far as the material goes, I have more memories of this class than any other at NYU.  Like the time unger sneezed and his "capillaries burst" and he taught the remainder of the class with a severe noseblee

Who is this guy kidding?  This is one of the most pompous professors I've ever had.  His book, "Living High and Letting Die", cloaked as something new to the field of ethics, is really just a weak attempt at modern utilitarianism.  If you take his class, get ready not to learn about ethics, but to buy his book and hear him talk about himself.

This is man is very brilliant, and very stubborn. He will argue a point with a student until he wins. It is an entertaining class. He teaches with his feet kicked up on his desk, and doesnt hesitate to close his eyes for long periods of time while lecturing. 3 Essays + participation in recitation. I am really glad i took this class, I recommend it.

His zoom lectures consist of him on his bed ranting out stuff that makes zero sense. When you try to talk ethics to him, he tells you not to talk technical. All his philosophical assumptions are based on thin air. Take this course if you're curious how tenured profs can get away w their bs.

ESL students dedicate their lives to learn a totally different language from their mother tongue to communicate and learn from people in the U.S. However,  He does not show any appreciation for their effort as an "Ethic Professor". He ignores students with an accent, even saying he doesn't understand what they are saying, but that is not true!

analysis.name: Usman Liaquat
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: ILRID 2510, explains diversity/discrimination but in a very scientific phycological way which I found very interesting. Less about personal experience more about how you're brain functions. Usman himself was very very generous, constantly bumping up the grades. Also very knowledgeable on the subject matter and was enthusiastic about class!

Had professor Liaquat on his first semester at Cornell for ILRID2500 and he absolutely killed it. Great slides, great lectures, fun readings, know when to assign long vs short readings. Take home quizzes that were perfectly reasonable. Has great character and charisma and is truly interested in what he teaches. Cannot recommend his class enough!

I had Usman for summer session one. He is super kind & compassionate. Always thinking about how to really help his students and make their lives better. He did his best every class to make the lectures engaging and was honestly a great guy. I learned a lot and I'm happy I had him as a professor because he truly does care. The class wasn't too hard!

Easily one of the best profs I've ever had! Managed to make 3hr lectures super engaging. Cares about students' learning over grades, generous w extra cred. Talented presenter, you'll understand even the most complex things with his teaching/explanations. Incredibly kind person/great lectures. Enough work to make you study, but not enough to stress.

Prof. Liaquat was great. His lectures were super interesting, and he made the content fun to learn about. Lecture heavy, a few quizzes, midterm and final. The class went really fast, so you had to stay on top of studying.

analysis.name: Ulrich Baer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: An Easy A Core Class. Do not be intimidated by the course name! The reading was minimal (if not enjoyable and informative)-15-30 pgs PER WEEK. The lectures were extremely entertaining, and he often ended early, which was nice. The prof is super chill, funny, knowledgeable, and accesible.There's lots of American history, if you like that, too.
Such a great professor! He is very accomodating to different kinds of students and will help you as best as he can if you just talk to him. Highly recommend!

Before you met him, Prof Baer at first appear to be a overtly liberal professor. Once you met him, you realize he is just a very kind, intelligent person. Eventually, you will realize his ideas actually make sense. His class contributes to a significant change of my view on the interaction between cultures. Strongly recommended for personal growth.

For an Expressive Culture class, this was surprisingly interesting. Baer introduces lots of intriguing discussions, and analysis on the texts (which are all very short) leave you thinking. For the essays, Baer lets you rewrite after he comments because he cares less about giving bad grades and more about your improvement as a writer. He's great!

Amazing professor. Very interesting person and extremely interesting lectures. Engages with the class and takes time to get to know the students. Provides plenty of opportunities for his students in and out of the class. Sometimes a little unclear on the assignments, but if you're focused and structured and willing to learn, you should get an A.

analysis.name: Phillip Usher
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: took fysem w him, rlly chill when it comes to discussions & flexible w projects/papers. the class is basically watching a movie per week & filling out a reflection so it doesnt take too much of ur time. theres 2 presentations, a midterm, and a final but all are easy to do well in. def one of the more interesting fysem classes so highly recommend

Professor Usher is so chill. He was the professor for First Year Seminar and the semester is literally you watching Spielberg films of various types and filling out a straight forward reflection for each. There were two essays and solo presentations as well. However, Professor Usher is incredibly understanding, and the semester was def memorable.
amazing professor! honestly such a fun class. no complaints.

Professor Usher is an amazing professor. He is one of my favorites among all of my French professors. He is funny, nice, and humorous. He allows for extra credits and he gives the topics for papers at the beginning of the semester. It is not really a heavy load class though he gives one quiz every week; but they are not hard at all.

analysis.name: Zach Udko
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 107 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He is one of the most influential teachers I have ever had. He changed the way I think of both my writing and myself. Zach really cared and it made all the difference.

My personal experience was phenomenal. I was challenged more than any other class; and, frankly, I was satisfied more than any other class. Zach has helped me hone my writing skills, and his class has helped me grow as a person via a large number of mental breakdowns and severe existential art/essay-related crises.

Zach completely changed how I think about learning. He's so supportive and really wants us to develop our own ideas, which sounds really basic but is surprisingly rare. His class is a place where I always felt comfortable working through my work even when it wasn't finished or polished. Genuinely thoughtful feedback. Also very funny.

Took WTE second semester with Udko. Lowkey unsettling. Likes to make himself seem really cool by showing us all his connections to famous people and then having us read about them. Wasn't a fan of that at 9 in the morning. Has generally good feedback but doesn't trust students

Zach will put in the work for you if you put in the work for him. My writing improved vastly over the course of the semester and he made what could easily be a dreadful course engaging and meaningful.

analysis.name: Edgar Ulloa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I love Professor Edgar. I wish he was going to be here for longer than just a year. I have loved his class and he is a fantastic person and teacher. I cannot wait to take him next semester!
Edgar is the best Spanish professor ever. He makes class so fun and enjoyable. He's easily accessible outside of class and will help out in any way possible. Would take this class again!
Proffesor is very knowledgeable and gives you a real experience with the language. Shares much insight with spanish culture and makes class fun to attend
Teaches you how to really speak Spanish, very verbal class not just textbook work. Would highly recommend.
From Mexico and teaches you how to really speak the language!!! Not just straight form book. Real world

analysis.name: Carlos Veloso Do Silva
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Veloso is the best ever. Like many of us I was not excited about the language requirement, but he makes class so fun I actually enjoy going. Even though there's no way he could know this, I am going through a really rough time right now and he has gone above and beyond to help me and be understanding. Just a great teacher & awesome guy.

I took SPAN-UA  1 with him and he was very funny and always made the class engaging. Some of his jokes were a bit weird at first but it actually made class more enjoyable! He always emphasizes that he is available to help students and made sure to answer every student's questions.
My favorite professor!!! Very kind and funny. Always there to help and wants to see his students succeed. Love him!
Had him for SPAN-UA 1, but it was not an option. He's so funny and good at his job. Everyone loved him in my class.

He is super weird and made sexual jokes during class which weren't funny and just made people uncomfortable. I didn't find the way he taught to be very helpful either, the textbook used was probably about 40 years old and it was Portugal Portuguese rather than Brazilian (90% of worldwide use), which makes no sense to teach in the United States.

analysis.name: Fred Ulfers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Ulfers is honestly really sweet and his class is very easy to get a good grade in if you listen to the lectures and take some notes. A lot of people zone out a couple of times but still take notes. The notes and handouts really help with writing his essays and understanding chiasmic unity. I'm glad I took his class.

I love Prof Ulfers. He is the sweetest man you'll ever meet. He is subtly funny, passionate about the readings in class, and extremely caring and understanding towards his students. W/ Covid he has been optimistic & helpful with paper extensions, generous with office hours & is just a lovely person. Would recommend his first-year seminar for sure!

Legend. Currently, my favorite professor at NYU. He's extremely intelligent, he'll understand any situation his students may encounter and will accommodate deadlines for you. To succeed, you must take notes during lectures on the concepts he talks about. Don't bother reading the classic novels, instead read the Word Docs & PDF files he emails you.
changed my life with his kindness and generosity of spirit, when he was my dean.

Haha, the grandfather comparison is accurate. He's an incredibly nice guy, and despite the size of the class, always pretty available to talk to. A really interesting lecturer, though he tends to ramble a bit. Has a fascinating way of looking at philosophy and literature, and the course reflects this. (Note: You'll be graded by a TA because of the class size.)

analysis.name: Joe Versoza
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

One of my favorite professors I taken at Stern! Class is always fun and the lectures include activities that always keep you invested. Exams are easy and he makes sure to not overwhelm you with work. Take his class if you can!

Sal provides engaging classes and many opportunities to participate and work with others you do not usually sit with or know. After all, you do not get to choose who you work with in a work setting.

analysis.name: Abigail Joseph

FYSEM Historical Fictions:

I really enjoyed my semester with Professor Joseph. She made class interesting, and she made a required course a little more bearable. The content is still difficult. analysis.name: Afrodesia McCannon

This is too much factual information to remember for a college-level class. Unclear guidelines and due dates. We have to take notes without knowing what is important for the test. Not inspirational at all. We should be practising critical thinking, but we're not. Can NYU provide more options for summer courses, please?

analysis.name: Maria Abascal

Professor Abascal is a good professor. However this lecture is 3 hours long once a week and is incredibly hard to sit through. She is good at explaining it though. Amazing. Material is extremely difficult, but he knows this and encourages questions and office hours visits, even if you ask the same question 15 times. analysis.name: Aaron Reliford

analysis.name: Ron Christie
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of those teachers that has so much to say he ends up on tangents a lot (in a good way). Textbooks but if you don't do the reading it makes no difference. A Republican but he's aware of his audience so it's never overbearing. Genuinely loves teaching. Make sure he knows your face and you'll get an A. Never gives grades though so that's annoying

Interesting course on the presidency, great content and the professor has many unique stories because of his personal background. Very caring professor. The only concern is that we never received any grades back except for our final grade. Seems tough to get a A but relatively easy to get an A-.

Christie's stories about his time in government really elevate the class material, and he makes the classroom environment very engaging. He's also well connected and will always help you get the contacts you need. Took almost an entire month to grade papers and post final grades on Albert

analysis.name: Aaron Gurwitz
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. is there for you, when you ask. Shares personal stories and is funny. Attend lectures to get a good midterm grade, memorise dates, etc. Expectations regarding the paper are unclear, but you learn to think for yourself and grading is fair!

Stay clear. Unless you like writing papers at a 300 level standard in a 200 level class with very little guidance, this is not the class for you. Gurwitz is a nice man and can be pretty funny at times, but his expectations are not clear. What is expected of you isn't clear and students use to grinding out numbers in other classes will be stumped.

Prof. is funny and helpful, replies to emails quickly. Midterm is tough indeed, but counts only 20% towards final grade; you have to memorize dates, attendance to class is useful as he asks things which are not in the slides. Grading on the paper is fair; little guidance and unclear expectations, but you learn to think for yourself!

Doesn't matter how well you do on the test since your grade is entirely based on the paper, with your midterm and final ending up to not matter much at all. He seems like a nice enough guy, funny and replies to his email quickly enough, except his grading on the paper is the harshest I've ever seen. Avoid.

Extremely unhelpful and unclear as to what he expects re: papers, assignments. The midterm for this past spring 14 was strictly memorizing dates-- very little comprehension of themes in his class was necessary. Would avoid 100%.

analysis.name: Aaditya Rangan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: In this class, you'l learn everything except for calculus. I now consider myself an expert on board game-playing neural networks, the different methods of transporting giant stone statues, and the various parasites that infect seagulls, but I do not know how to take a derivative.

Professor Rangan is a true gem. His lectures are always clear and concise and he does a remarkable job of explaining the real world application of the concepts that he is teaching. Homework is graded for completion and there are no quizzes. The exams are straight from the homework and open note. We took his final instead of the departmental one.

He did NOT teach us anything we needed to know for Calc II. He taught everything conceptually and graphically and I left that class not knowing how to solve a single equation. I got an A. He literally counted the dept final as a quiz and made his own final to get away with it. Now I'm behind in all of my chemistry courses bc can't do the math

aaditya rangan is so hilarious that my chest hurts from laughing so much during the lecture. he always keeps his lectures clear and concise, and always tells really funny stories. overall, he is a solid guy. he does not follow the book at all, but instead teaches us real world application. there is minimal homework and open note tests.
Rangan is absolutely terrible. Don't take him if you want to retain your sanity.

analysis.name: Aaron Balkan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Aaron is a cool dude.  To be honest, I liked him a lot better in retrospect.  He knows his stuff and he is pretty reasonable.  He has a cool, though dry, sense of humor and he is very relatable, especially to film students.  If you have him, check out his website aaronbalkan.com.  Make a comment about one of his films or poems to earn some points

He has a wry and sarcastic sense of humor that can come across as mean, but it's alright. Really, the problem is that he's vague, vague to the point of confusion about what it is HE wants YOU to do. I'm willing to accept that I need to improve, but I'd prefer to be told HOW.  He's a good teacher when reveiwing one-on-one, but too abstract in class

Many ppl don't like him, but I really liked his class. Not having him 2nd sem was a bit harder. His movie knowledge was so interesting! I always wrote down his suggestions. Sometimes his directions were vague, but in the end he made me into a much better writer. You just have to be willing to put in a ton of work into your essays and exercises.

The class itself is terrible, but there's no way to change that. Aaron's a really nice guy and a fairly easy grader. He doesn't always give a lot of feedback unless you ask for it, but if you do, he's pretty helpful. He's a good guy and a good teacher but he needs to have more classroom discussions cause otherwise everyone just spaces out.

I did pretty well in & liked HS English but WTE was more about thinking. Always interesting,but hard. Wish I had done better/had more time on some of my essays--usually by the time I turned them in I felt like I was just getting started. Aaron was cool teacher-unexpected humor & knew lots of cool film & music.

analysis.name: Adam Meyers
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Adam is very kind as a person and is easy to approach and talk to. However, as a professor, his teaching style results in extremely tedious and dull lectures that ultimately have turned me away from the subject matter. His lectures are unbelievably monotonous and hard to follow. Homeworks are long and tedious. Exams are a breeze.

He is probably the best professor out there in NYU. Really lenient on grading criteria and you just have to go to every class and do the problem sets and you will do well. Quizzes get dropped, problem sets get dropped and even one of the two midterms too if you do bad on one. Finals matter the most.

Having his background in linguistics, he is keen on making python feel useful and accessible to non-stem or non-comp sci majors. Really nice guy. Lectures can get dull sometimes, but he tends to use good examples. Average difficulty homework and exams. The general feel of the class was very laid back. Would take him again!
Amazing plethora and range of Hawaiian shirts.

Very good professor, focuses on learning rather than memorizing, lenient grader. Homeworks are not reaally easy but doable and not that long. All the help is provided in the prompt such as how to approach the problem.

analysis.name: Adam Pincus
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed biz of film. He is a really good lecturer and I actually really enjoyed his class. 3 papers 1 midterm exam, I honestly don't think its too hard if you went to class regularly. But Prof. Pincus seems to be not so accessible outside of class. But he is a nice guy and feels approachable. Recommend for those who took movie marketing.
So chill & he cares. I took this class for J term and really enjoyed it. He can get a bit technical with the business side of things, but I did learn a lot and a fun class to talk film!
I recommend this class. He's a good guy and great at answering questions on confusing topics. Enjoyed this class.
genuinely chill dude. super friendly and knowledgeable about the film industry.

Prof. Pincus is very experienced and knowledgeable in the Business of Film, and his lectures were different and interesting. Pop quizzes did make for a more difficult class than expected, but he expects hard work, and that's motivating. Lectures were up-to-date and relevant, with exciting film info. Good balance of sarcastic and serious. Recommend.

analysis.name: Adina Schick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 91 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Teaching style is very bland - Dr. Schick essentially just takes her slides word-for-word from the online textbook and recites them during lecture. Attendance is mandatory because of online polling questions. The professor makes comments such as "if you get this question wrong, you don't deserve to pass the exam" & is not accessible for help.

Professor Schick has been quite awful. As a lecturer, she is very clear, but as a professor has little interaction with the students. The TAs handle all the work, and while I was lucky to have a good TA, Prof. Schick was the opposite. She goes too fast at times, and her exams do not correlate much with the lectures, but with the readings instead.

As a scholar, Dr.Schick was doing her job. But as a professor/dean of APUG, she tends to exhibit a low tolerance for mistakes and high egocentricity. When I fail anything, talking with her makes me feel panicky and self-loathed, and always puts me in an anxious mood. Like even a small mistake can end up in some catastrophic results.

Arrogant, uninterested, and completely inaccessible for help. Lectures are as dry and boring as can be, might as well just read the slides yourself. Absolutely miserable prof and class, highly recommend against taking.

she's the worst professor ever and is being very strict on attendance. I only missed 1-2 polls per class since I had some tech issues or i wasn't able to react and she gave me a very bad grade for participation.

analysis.name: Adam Brown
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: When the Nightmare is Real/child trauma psych. Really interesting class, used visuals and great examples to make it all very comprehensible. Readings were kind of long, but you can just skim them.
Turn in your work on time and you'll be fine. Lots of reading but quizzes are easy. Brown is really chill and incredibly knowledgeable in his field.

Professor Brown was great. He clearly cares about the topic he teaches and makes complex topics easier to understand. The midterm and final were online, in class, in a lockdown browser (but since we had to write a lot, it made it easier). You don't have to read the books to write the essays.

Very interesting lessons, with amazing and interactive guest speakers! He's super nice and caring and easy to talk to. Though the grading on the midterms and final was a bit ehh, super specific for no reason. Just be sure to REALLY study.

He's a little strict but it's very obvious this is a class that matters a lot to him. In a few classes he's talked about his own experience working with traumatized children. I felt bad because barely anyone participated. His assignments are also writing-heavy but on really fascinating books! His midterm was difficult for me but his final was easy!

analysis.name: Adam Becker
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very passionate about his subject. The course is focused on ancient Christian history, and the texts can be hard to follow. If you're not already interested in religious topics, staying engaged can be tough, but he explains things clearly and wants students to succeed. Lectures are mostly discussion and explanation-based based with a few slides.

Professor Becker is so awesome, and I loved this class so much. The readings were so interesting, and I couldn't stop thinking about dedicating my life to monasticism even months after the class ended. I'm honestly still thinking about it.

just finished final, not bad at all. introduced a new grading scheme this year that's basically just completion, super easy to get a good grade as long as you do (most of) the readings and review. extremely smart, absurdly knowledgeable on super niche things. class is a little vague/unstructured, but if you're mostly locked in you'll be okay.

A chill guy. Definitely haunted by some personal demons. His lectures are kind of played by ear and a bit unstructured, but its very clear he is passionate about what he teaches. There were a lot of readings, so be sure to sign up for this course only if you're willing to put the effort into each text.

Prof Becker is a class act, highly witty, incredibly knowledgeable on a wide range of subjects, a cunning linguist, approachable and deeply humane. You can tell he's smoked a few doobies in his time too; he's like .. way chilled and stuff. And he's got a twinkle in his eye.

analysis.name: Adam Roddy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Such a fun class! I was delighted every day that I stepped foot into this lecture. Truly you must take him as a professor if you want the true NYU experience. He is also HILARIOUSSSS and a joy to be around and takes the content seriously, but makes everything engaging for his students. If he taught all classes at NYU, I would be there immediately.

Professor Roddy is a fantastic lecturer and a caring mentor. The criteria for grading was clear and always consistent. Besides attendance, homework is graded generously and the final project is really what determines your class grade. He makes intimidating material very easy to understand and he's very funny!

Professor Roddy is awesome! I knew nothing about coding at first and struggled, but he was always patient and willing to explain things multiple times. He's approachable outside of class, genuinely wants to help students, grades fairly, and has a great sense of humor with lots of stories. Take him !

Take him! Even for people who don't have interest in computer programming or writing codes like me learned a lot. He is funny, having clear ideas not to lower down grades but teach some real stuff. No tests, but assignment weekly+final pre/paper. Not too much workload, no pressure. Just do your work and show up, the TA is awesome.

analysis.name: Adriana Garcia Garcia
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Clearly a smart person however does not know how to properly run a class. Extremely disorganized and graded purely on three tests that you will have no idea how they are graded or what she is looking for. Lectures are sometimes engaging but mostly bad and she makes students feel stupid when they speak in class. TA's particularly bad in this class!

This is my favorite class I've taken at NYU! It's not a class for people who want to zone off and still do well and participation is important. The class discussions and activities, the cases she chooses, and the points she raises are all insightful and engaging. The exams are not that difficult as long as you study and pay attention in class.

Usually I don't trust bad reviews on here, but she is really not a good professor. Not necessarily difficult to do well, but lectures are tedious and I didn't learn anything new about the constitution. Slow to grade, unclear on expectations, very disorganized. Avoid if you can!

I had a really great semester taking Prof Garcia's SCOTUS class. Her grading is fair and she is open to criticism. I actually liked the Socratic method, and thought it was cool to hear from my peers. She is clearly very intelligent and cares a lot about her students. If you go to class and pay attention, you will get the A! Would recommend to all!

Prof as a person seems nice and smart but I did not like her style of teaching. "Lectures" are just conversation with the few loud people in class (bc of so-called socratic method), and I'm not paying 90k tuition because I care about their opinions. Not a fan of grading system: 30% Midterm 1, 30% Midterm 2, 40% Final. TAs disorganized & grade slow.

analysis.name: Aimee Cox
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: PROF COX IS AWESOMEEE. Best core class I have ever taken. The material is so interesting and she truly cares about students beyond class. She makes an effort to go outside the classroom and take us to see dance. She prioritizes our own mental health and wellbeing as well! Prof Cox is literally the best professor you could ask for!

Had her for Anthro of Black Dance. The course is reading-heavy, but they're not difficult and are summarized in recitations. Her lectures seemed to be a little all over the place at times. I got lost at times, but I feel like the midterm and final are not difficult if you pay attention most of the time in class.

Amazing professor, first time I felt very engaged in the class during my time at NYU. There is a lot of readings and material from lecture you need to study, but besides that the class is a breeze. Def take!
Prof Cox is very passionate and knowledgable about what she teaches and makes the lectures highly engaging. Its not difficult to do well in this class, just engage with the material well!

analysis.name: Adrian Versteegh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super smart. Looks like a young Brad Pitt. Holds class in the park when the weather is nice. What's not to love?

One of the smartest people I have ever met... awesome lecturer... seems intimidating at first but is actually genuinely kind and sweet. Helps a lot during office hours. And yes I would totally have his blue eyed babies.

This was easily one of the best classes I've taken. Adrian is a talented lecturer and engaging discussion leader, very generous with his time and willing to accommodate different student interests. Obviously the two negative reviews below were written by the same person. But Adrian gets a lot of attention. That's probably why you're here, right? ;)

Taking him now for Victorian Literature. Adrian is an amazing, knowledgeable instructor. He always comes prepared and is a great discussion leader. A bit challenging, but you will do well as long as you read, participate and do the assignments. Caring. Understanding. And, yes, the man is jaw-droppingly handsome. If I could... let me stop.

He is seriously smart on an array of topics and can sometime seem intimidating. However, as long as you read, everything will be swell. People tend to describe him as boring and not good at leading class discussions but he is in fact the opposite. He is able to lecture to a class full of students who did read and that's a true talent.

analysis.name: Ailis Cournane
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If you are taking First Lang. Acq. as a linguistics major then this class will be a breeze. There are 2 hws, a midterm, a final and a project. Exams are fair. The project isn't horrible. There are weekly readings, but Ailis lectures almost directly from the book so you don't have to do them. She's very smart, nice, and approachable. Loves questions

First Lang Acq was a really fun class. If you're a linguistics major, you get some extra room to breathe b/c the psych people have to learn IPA stuff and what morphemes are and w/e. I would have liked more assignments and more feedback, but it was a solid class. The midterm was very short and very specific, but the final grade composition is good.

Ailis is a great teacher! She made all classes interesting and engaging. It was her first time teaching at NYU and she did a great job. Though I believe this class is an easy A, you need to work hard for your grade. There is no midterm. However, be ready for a final exam, a short paper, seven online quizzes, and two short assignments. Great class!

I took her Language and Mind class online. It can be a bit boring and hard to follow for non-linguistic majors or if you're not particularly interested in the subject, but she was a good lecturer and her class was easy enough to follow. She clearly knows a lot about her field.

I took this class she taught with McElree and it was very unenjoyable. Prof C is a great lecturer and really knows what she is talking about, however, in conjunction with the poorly teaching from the other professor as well as the general lack of time management, I do not recommend taking P27. I would, however, take a class just taught by Prof C.

analysis.name: Rita Aiello
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She does want her students to think, yet she stifles what everyone has to say with some research that SHE has conducted already.(sometimes missing your point completely) She has a huge ego. I certainly wanted to learn and work and didn't expect an easy A, but she was very reluctant to help and listen. She has biases towards some students. MusicPsyc

She's very nice & genuine. If you write about something that is important and meaningful and is compatible with the content it's an easy A. Only two papers and a presentation for the entire semester... but a LOT of readings. She goes through each reading during class so I wouldn't say it's completely necessary, but participation helps boost grade.

I loved this Professor. The students that complain about her are most likely "idiots" just because she wants her students to "think" she is hailed as this horrible professor. I really enjoyed her class and I learned a great deal. Take this class if you are not afraid of learning by working and are not in it for an easy A.

What an incredible professor! Rita explained psycholinguistics to the class in ONE lecture, and before that I wasted a whole semester trying to understand it in Brian McElree's class. That said, she's a great teacher. What an asset to NYU.Very fun class, lots of reading, but you'll learn tons. One of the best psych class I took @ NYU! I miss her!

She gives 100 pages to read each week with an optional extra 100 pages that are not optional at all, dont let the optional fool you. All of this doesnt even matter to her, she chose your grade the moment you stepped in her class and will grade you accordingly. She does not like minorities and people who speak an opinion opposing hers. Dont take

analysis.name: Allison Aitken
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a great person, but lectures are boring, and there's no space for debating philosophical topics; the focus is on how they are argued. I didn't do the readings in the first half of the semester, got a B on the midterm, did them in the second half and still got a B on the final. I am a good writer and have all A's in humanities classes. Beware

prof aitken is really great! granted how the thick material and readings are, she makes it very comprehendible. super open to help, office hours were always so helpful. lectures were sometimes really hard to stay engaged in, but i think thats just a product of zoom. she generally made philosophy soooo much less daunting, and workload wasnt crazy

Prof Aitken is great! SO sweet and always accessible for help. Deadlines are pretty fixed but imo, they're super generous so even if you can't get an extension you'll still probably finish on time. I was a bit scared to take the class bc she was a new teacher without a rep, but I am so glad I decided to take it bc she is such a gem
really good prof, lectures entertaining even if material is dense and difficult. pretty easy grading, exams were not too hard either. readings can be skipped, lectures provide what you need

analysis.name: Rodolfo Aiello
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: What a grumpy old man!  He's so mean and bitter all of the time I actually began to dread class in preparation for what mean things he would say to me. However, he did improve my Spanish skills and understanding immensely. He was very smart and had a good sense of humor.  He really made Spanish class an awful experience three times a week.

I think few people realize that his class is supposed to separate the wheat from the chaff. He expects a little discipline, to be sure, but my grammar was pretty much flawless by the end of the semester. An A is not impossible if you make an effort.

He has good days and bad days.  He's definitely a moody person, but he's good at teaching and really knows a lot.  I was lazy and never came to class with the exercises done and he never cared.  He even gave me chances to turn stuff in late.
Professor Aiello was extremely helpful and hilarious.  He was extremely knowledgeable and his mood swings aren't that bad.  He's very nice especially during office hours, very hospitable.

The absolute worst professor I hope to have in my college experience. Often came to class late, impossible to understand, often canceled or rescheduled class, ridiculed students, didn't explain or answer questions. One of the reasons I am not studying spanish anymore. He said he was retiring at the end of last fall, but apparently he's back. beware

analysis.name: Aisha Khan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: class involves 4 exams that involve the readings, so get ready to MEMORIZE. she does put a lot of resources on brightspace on what you actually need to know, so lecture is kind of just repeating that. overall nice lady and did offer to help people in separate office hours just for exams.

Prof Khan's class is boring and not what you think: 1-2 classes learning of indigenous peoples, rest based on colonization. Class is based on 4 essays (not hard), but the prompts can be very vague and open ended. Most frustrating parts: lectures w ridiculous tangents; you have to get a 95 to get an A (you can get a 94 on every essay and get an A-)

The TA's are amazing, but Mrs. Khan's teaching style is so hard to follow. She refuses to use powerpoints and instead repeats herself constantly, calling out students, who need to use the restroom, as irresponsible. If you have an opinion that is different than hers, good luck. She knows a lot about the subject, but you seem to learn nothing.

She's super interactive and passionate but she repeats herself and rambles a lot. No power points, just lectures and readings. Your grade is based only on 4 exams, making this a hard class if you don't test well. Made tests purposefully hard, but you receive exam prompts a week in advance to prepare.

She's friendly & passionate but she can be quite repetitive during lectures, and will tend to ramble on and on, maybe go off topic. She does not believe in power points either, which will make lectures kind of dense but honestly what you really need is just to read what's assigned and it will be an easy A.

analysis.name: Berfu Aygenc Akman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very sweet and does not ask much of you other than to participate in class. Has 4 homework assignments you have to do for chapter readings. Doesn't like tests so only has a midterm which is very easy if you do homework and listen to lectures. Final paper is also easy. Class is long but she does her best to never keep you the entire time.
Easy A take it if you want gpa boosts

The LIGHTEST class you will ever take. Two presentations, and online midterm, and online final paper (short). The lecture is long but its okay for the amount of work you have to do. If youre gonna take intro to sociology TAKE HER!!!!

She is a great professor!! So sweet! Was always open for questions and helping us for future exams/papers. I had a class right before this one and I was presenting a final Project for that class right before her final exam. She offered to delay the exam 5 mins which i declined but she was so understanding w/ everything.

She is truly a wonderful professor. She cares a lot about sociology and she makes it enjoyable and easy. There are only 4 assignments to do and they are very easy and worth 20% of your final grade. She loves hearing about what you have to say and does whatever to make people feel comfortable enough to participate. Easy midterm and easy final paper.

analysis.name: Asif Akhtar
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Provided late feedback and it was often unclear. never gave rubrics or assignments sheets so directions were confusing. When asked questions about assignments he wouldn't clarify. Class was suppose to be discussion based but he would go on rants for anywhere from 20-40 minutes . Final paper: 12-15 pages, over 100 pages a week to read

Lots of dense, theoretical readings (100s of pages a week) and will assign films to watch the night before class. No rubric or instructions for assignments. He's a nice guy and seems to care about his students but the workload was far too heavy and he rambles quite a lot in class.

Prof Akhtar is a tough teacher but wants his students to learn the course material well and hence assigns a lot of reading but the guest lectures were a great way to hear about practicing artists working with some of the technologies in the readings.

analysis.name: Adwoa Akhu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dont take her; if necessary, wait until the following term to take the course. This instructor does not have regards for students and how her actions will impact their future. She can fail students over minor mistakes. Also, she can fail students after the term is over regardless of completion of all assignments and internship site hours.

Do not take this class if you want to have peace of mind and do well. This professor fails students at the last minute for arbitrary and minor reasons despite telling them they are doing well thoughout the semester. She makes you write so much and is harshly critical. I heard someone had to go to the ER due to the stress of Akhu.
Do not take this professor by any means. I got an A in the mid-term but unexpectedly, she failed me the class after the term was over. Also, she is rude, dismissive, and hardly teaches.

analysis.name: Anna Akbari
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tough, but fair. She really loves the subject. Lots of reading, but it's the sort of stuff you'd probably keep on your shelf after graduation to impress people.  Also, I feel bad about saying this given the content of the class, but Prof. A is hot, and I'm not talking teacher hot, straight up hot.

I've taken two classes with Anna. Incredible instructor/person––passionate, knowledgeable, and so interesting. If you are looking for an easy A, this is not the class for you. If you are looking to grow academically, intellectually, personally, socially--& willing to put in the work––her classes will give you that. Also ditto the hot comment above.

class was sometimes interesting but it was a mistake to take. tons of reading and work every week. tons of field research for a huge paper at the end. no tests but a lot of responses and field work. shes crazy into the subject but everything comes from the readings. has nothing to do with comm so i dont know why its an ILA - all sociology.

She was right on top of things! Led me through the curriculum like she was born to teach. Would have appreciated a bit more performance feedback, but overall a solid, hard-working, dedicated, erudite star in her field-versatile and a consumate risk-taker. Highly recommended!

analysis.name: Linell Ajello
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't trust old reviews—her grading changed. The “grading contract” is vague and you will not know your grade until you recieve it at the end. Incompletes drop your grade a full letter, & marked unfairly. Extra credit? Don't expect to get it if you do it. Excused absences count as absences. I took this class so you don't have to. Don't.

girl do not walk but RUN in the other direction. if you can take bio off track I would because this is the TRENCHES. she has called students stupid on multiple occasions, teaches the content ineffectively, and writes exam questions that are unclear. words cannot describe how bad of a teacher she is. bout to have me like kendrick on drake.

Prof. Bloomberg's courses are the future of CS education. NYU promote this man before MIT recruits him, lol.
