Something I disliked was that it was easy for our class discussions to veer off course: one class we spent almost an hour looking for cafes on the Upper East Side. Overall, great!

Elaine is such a caring professor--- not only does she care for all of her students but she's incredibly passionate/ wise regarding the work she's doing in & out of the classroom. She is also just an incredibly understanding human who knows how stressful school/ life can be and doesn't push too hard in her efforts to get the best work out of you.

Although Professor Ayers has made efforts to being nice and organize her classroom, it has not been entirely successful. The course content has been lengthy and unengaging. Her grading process has not been timely, which has added to my frustration. LOTS OF READINGS, which has made it challenging to maintain interest in the subject matter.

analysis.name: Aya Matsushima
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: At first, Matsushima seems very professional, but is very patient and helpful if you need anything inside or outside of class. In language classes, the easiest teachers don't always help you learn, and I'd rather have a prof w/ high expectations than not learn the language. She may seem demanding, but is understanding and never criticizes mistakes.

She is a really talented teacher. She is always there to help her students. She is available in her office and through email. She is approachable and very understanding. But like the class requires, she does go by the textbook and attendance is required. I must say she ranks  number 1 on my list for teaching Japanese. She is awesome.

She's a lot of fun to have a class with because of her youth and understanding of modern Japanese culture. You can tell her experience from teaching comes from enjoying the learning process, and you can tell her roots are very Japanese in nature. She's a lovely teacher and outside of class a respectable person all around.

She's incredibly arrogant and strict.  She does not create a warm learning environment and my classmates and I agreed that we hated volunteering and answering questions when she was teaching the class.  I'm surprised at the good reviews, because I've had to deal with her cranky attitude for two semesters in a row.

Very helpful and fun.  She has a professional air and may seem strict, but is actually very nice in person.  The tests are ok, but there is a lot of homework.  She teaches out of the book so it's very easy to keep up.

analysis.name: Ayda Erbal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ayda is clearly very intelligent but the class is way too much. The amount of reading assigned is overwhelming, which is obvious since she only is able to cover about 50% of it during class lectures. Your entire grade is based off basically just the final and midterm; the grading for those is insane. The class is super informative but at what cost

Ayda is extremely knowledgable about what she teaches,  but can often be incoherent and extremely disorganized.  She was constantly behind on the syllabus and didn't upload a missing lecture until the night before the midterm.  Wish she could get herself together a little more because she has a lot of knowledge to share.

DO NOT TAKE. SO DIFFICULT. THE WORKLOAD IS JUST INSANE. if you're interested in the topic, then read about it on your own time. don't subject yourself to this class. everyone i talked to regretted taking it. i'm just saying

I took Democracy and Dictatorship as well as International Politics of the Middle East. Ayda is a crazy genious but she will be as demanding to you as she is to herself. She is caring and her classes are the most interesting you will ever take. However, dont think for a second she will write you a recommendation letter -  she's so unreliable!

Professor Erbal is scary smart and really knows her stuff on Middle Eastern politics.  The class isn't easy, and there are A LOT of dense readings (most of which you do need to do).  Her explanations of the readings were a little incoherent at times, but she was always willing to answer questions when students had them.

analysis.name: Maha Aziz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is very helpful, she always brings speakers and guests who also suggested internships to us. She is very helpful not only as a professor but also as a connection and a reference!
The best classes I have ever taken at NYU
My recommendation to take her classes!
Best professor at the IR department

Professor Aziz is a great professor. I took her class on Political Risk and Prediction at NYU. Her lectures are structured, and engaging. Expect a lot of group discussions and presentations. She gives her students a lot of intellectual freedom and does not expect them to adhere to a single school of thought. She is very accessible outside class.

analysis.name: Habib Azar
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really like Habib! He truly cares about his students and he wants them to make their best work! He's a very nice guy and he knows his stuff. Sometimes he can say some questionable things but other than he's pretty chill. He gives good feedback on your work and he is always willing to lend a helping hand in the Studio.

I learned SO MUCH in this class. This professor knows a ton about Studio sets and how to run them. Though this professor does make you work for it to get things done accurately and efficiently, I can definitely say that it has improved my filmmaking skills so much over this past semester. 10/10 would take again!

I was nervous when I saw that he had no ratings but Habib is literally one of the most passionate, knowledgeable, and sweetest sight and sound professors you could ever have. I definitely recommend him for studio.

analysis.name: Azeez Bhavnagarwala
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: put little to minimal effort to teaching and it shows. always late to class, confusing and wrong answer keys and questions. His labs and homeworks can sometimes take hours and hours to do and he asks materials that havent been covered yet in his assignments. If you learn everything on your own good grades are very possible but dont rely on him

Took the CSA course as one of my core requirements.
It's my first Sem here at NYU. Professor seems very knowledgeable & helpful with any doubts. He gives all the right info and material. He's approachable via mail. The TA is super kind and explains patiently.
Overall the course seems very good for your first Sem to get eased into the program.

He's very disorganized professor who dont put that much effort into running the class for better or worse. For the worse: his assigned labs and hws take hours and hours to finish and everyone request extensions every single week. For the better: his exam looks like he wrote it an hour before so its not bad if you study the materials yourself.

Professor Bhavnagarvala know his stuff and his vast experience in the industry gives his lectures an extra edge. He is always ready to help outside of class as well. His deep understanding of the subject brought a new and interesting way of looking at the subject.

Professor knows his stuff and is always ready to help his students. Course is structured to help students be competent in the industry. He also makes sure that every student in the class is upto speed with the course content.

analysis.name: Efrain Azmitia
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Azmitia is an excellent professor and lecturer. Be sure that you attend all lectures and lab sessions, and that you are highly familiar with the powerpoints. You will be tested monthly. If you have an average of "A" in his class (labs, papers, and tests combined), you will be exempt from taking the final exam. 4 tests, 2 papers, lab every week.

Not your typical MAP class. Consists of 4 tests in the semester, of which your top 3 count for 40% of your grade. Final (30%) is pretty much all repeated questions from those tests. Labs + 2 papers which count for 30% in all are a joke. The tests are really annoying, but not having to study for a final is nice. Graded fairly. Prob easiest NatSci II

His lectures were very disorganized and he can be rather confusing. The questions on the tests are taken directly from the powerpoints but the powerpoints often were out of context and didn't really make any sense. The tests always had mistakes on them which reflects how some of the TA's really didn't care. Overall, I regret taking this class.

Absolutely terrible! The worst class ever! I strongly recommend you to avoid his class (I feel terrible for saying this about his lecture) but it is true that he is just NOT good at teaching. The lectures are disorganized and he does not clarify what to study and what not to. I felt like he was rambling throughout the lectures. Don't take his class

He makes no sense, makes no effort to explain, the test are hard but subjected to an absurd curve in which 65-90 is a B, and it is impossible to get more than that. He spelled the same word 3 different ways in the same sentence. I have no words to describe what a failure at teaching this man is. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR NATSCI II,it was a mistake

analysis.name: Samantha Bassler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honestly I didn't learn a thing but Dr. Bassler is very funny and tries to be engaging. She would cancel all the time, often last minute and yap the entire time when we did have class. The homework assignments and quizzes weren't too bad as long has you somewhat knew the material beforehand. Lot's of dictation and unrelated conversation.

Lots of negativity among other reviews, which I think are unwarranted and unhelpful. Dr. Bassler is a knowledgeable and effective lecturer. However, she occasionally cancels lectures, which leads to either pivoting in assignments or the lecture schedulei tself. I did not feel that she did this intentionally, and she clearly communicated.

Thought it was a good class since my friend told me exams are online. However, this class is not worth it, it does not make sense how this 1-credit Aural class gave so much work every week, even more than my 1-credit Engineering class. Attendance mandatory. Grading for midterm and finals is not clear. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. DEF NOT A ONE CREDIT CLASS.
Took her aural and music history II. She has literally more absence than most of us do. Many excuses. No in-person exam though.

She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She will make sure that everyone gets the material. She does tend to cancel class quite a bit, but it's usually due to health issues which aren't her fault. If you want a professor that is genuinely passionate about what she's teaching, this is the one.

analysis.name: Danis Banks
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Good professor for writing. She gives thoughtful comments on your essays. Very tough on grammar and sentence structure. Would recommend if you're a capable writer. If you're looking for perfect grades every time leave. Participation is IMPORTANT

One of the best professor during my college career. Very knowledgeable, caring, and accessible. She is strict but I think this is beneficial for learning, which would be good for you unless you just want to take a easy course. Also a teacher that had very important education on me, very lucky for the experience of studying with Banks.

3 years after graduating college I came back to write this review for professor Banks. If there was one professor through my entire schooling career I actually remember, it's her. She's caring but more than anything her teaching style and overall content has been truly impactful in my life after college. I think of her often & hope she is well!!

3 papers and 1 group project. for my class: paper 1 was imitating the writing style of an author we studied in class paper 2 was an academic essay paper 3 was a personal essay. group project was to introduce a painting at a museum. project was super easy, pretty chill grader, hates tardiness, try to participate but lowkey it doesn't affect grade

She is just a Karen who only gives feedback on grammatical errors without constructive advice. TOUGH GRADER. I hate her. She is ruining my college experience. I wish that I had dropped this class the first day. Don't be deceived by the overall rating.

analysis.name: Jed Bernstein
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He has extensive experience in arts marketing and is highly passionate about his work. Be ready to participate in class, and he grades kindly. His lectures are very engaging, and he truly cares about ensuring his students understand the material. I definitely recommend!

Absolutely my favorite class/prof so far. As someone hoping to pursue a future in arts marking, I cant think of someone I'd want to learn from more than Jed. He has a fantastic knowledge of niche areas of the arts, and presents everything in a really clear and coherent way. He's also super fun and caring, and brings snacks often (!!!!!!)

I adore this man. My favorite professor so far in college. He taught me so much. His lectures are informative and he encourages participation. 2 essays and a final project. I met with him outside of class for career advice and he was helpful. He brings in industry professionals as guest lecturers.

The professor is very educated about theatre. But for me and many others who thought the class would be more art oriented, this is not a good class to take. In addition, the professor grades overly harsh on participation and attendance. Miss two classes? 67% on participation and attendance.

the GREATEST human being/professor to exist at NYU. he really cares about his students and goes above and beyond to show it (brings pizza/snacks to class and actually listens to us for feedback). i could go on and on about jed so if you have the chance TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!

analysis.name: Jay Van Bavel
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Im pre med taking orgo and phys and somehow this class was my lowest grade. His exams are in person open note which sounds easy but like half the exam is ultra specific questions that require a niche understanding of something mentioned once during a lecture. On our third midterm he asked questions about a 10 minute ted talk he played one time?????

I don't think it's worth taking this professor for Intro to Psych. Exams make up 90% of the grade, and the essay portion makes an A unlikely. First two exams had low average. There are other Intro Psych courses at NYU that are easier for earning high grades. im. a math major and this might be my lowest grade which is insane, DUMB GRADING AVOID!

Great Professor overall, but class is test havy 3 midterms and 1 final  account for 90% of your final grade and The final is optional if you do well on all 3 midterms. The average for the first midterm was an 80, so basically impossible to get an A? He says he will curve if the average is too low, but not sure how that is going to work out

Great professor! Although classes are online, he makes it very engaging and explains concepts throughly. 3 exams, 1 optional final that is cumulative but can replace an exam grade. You can bring any paper material you want to the exams which is helpful. Very nice and knowledgeable, lectures are all recorded too.

I absolutely love this professor!! He is the best professor I have had. I loved his classes and how he connected psych topics to pop references. His exams are not hard, but extremely specific, so you have to make good notes for your exams, which takes time. But I'd do it again if I had to.

analysis.name: Frances Bernstein
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If you value feedback, do not take this class. It is impossible to gauge your standing because she doesn't return assignments until the very end. The grading criteria is a moving target—different for every student—and her 'regrading' policy just adds to the confusion.

I absolutely LOVED Professor Bernstein. She cared so much about the subject and the students. She was always accessible outside of class (email, Zoom or office hours.) The class consisted of reading about 3 articles for each class, class participation/discussion (20%), 2 papers (one worth 10% and the other 20%), and a midterm (20%) and final (30%).
This course is primarily evaluated through two major written assignments.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Heard
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not at all a tough grader. With her, just do what she says and you'll do great. Unfortunately, that means EVERYTHING. You get 2 absences before it starts affecting your grade (which is ridiculous). Assignments are easy, but they're due at the dumbest times. Not a bad teacher though. Class was enjoyable. Material isn't even hard, just do it exactly.

The best professor ever at NYU!!! Easy greader, very sweet! Just do everything she said, and you will be fine with this class. Participation is important, but the discussion in class is fun and interesting.

I like the course but it was super group work heavy. If you're someone who prefers to work alone or is a control freak, then this course is kinda a nightmare. Heard is nitpicky and will find anything wrong with your assignment. I wouldn't say she's a tough grader though, just someone who strives for perfection, a know-it-all and annoying.

All assignments are group projects and your group is assigned by random and is the same for the entire semester. The professor is an easy grader and grades based on effort not quality; the projects are quite tedious and time-consuming though. The lectures are pretty boring but the class is an easy A as long as you submit your work on time.

I have taken 2 classes with her. Very clear grading criteria and if you follow her prompts you will get an A regardless of the quality. She is super knowledgeable and wise. I took her for communicating gender and identity and absolutely loved the class and the material especially the films.

analysis.name: Dhruva Bhaskar
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really liked his teachings, provides helpful videos prior to exams to help study really wants his students to learn the subject. Attendance not mandatory but I think going in and taking the EC quizzes were what saved me.

Very laid back, prof. Attendance is not mandatory at all. He teaches alright but sometimes makes a few mistakes here and there. He's quite forgiving on his exams as he gives big curves. 

The good thing is that he does an online review before each exam, with tons of practice questions that do help.
Great instructor. Concise lectures, easy to follow and understand. One of the best professors I've had!
He is a good professor overall, however, he can sometimes be unclear with his instructions.

analysis.name: Rajni Bhargava
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Take her for hindi class if you can. She is hilarious and so funny. I would only recommend if you have some knowledge of hindi or speak another language similar to it. Grade is dependent on trying to actually learn the language rather than perfection.
Auntieji is amazing and I love her. She's a great professor. Very nice. Explains things well. She doesn't believe in tests, so she actually just cares that you learn.

truly one of the best professors at nyu. she is so caring and truly wants everyone to learn. she is so funny but this class is not for true beginners. i would advise against the class if you cant speak even a little or even understand the language.

Prof truly cares about our learning and making sure we can apply material to real life. But Elementary is def not for pure beginners. Luckily I have a little background in Hindi but if you don't know an ounce of it, I wouldn't recc. This class is purely participation and group work, with lots of small assignments.
Professor Bhargava cares more about you learning the language than grading you harshly on small assignments. The class is very centered around participation so you need to attend all sessions.

analysis.name: Vivek Bhatt
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bhatt is a gem in the LS department! He cares a lot about student's opinions, but also gives good information making sure you can be prepared for the midterm/final if you pay attention. The midterm is an exam taken in class, but the final is a take home exam. The class is very discussion-based, but he's open to new ideas! TAKE HIM!!

I always looked forward to his class and it amazes me how he is fitted up every day. Pretty reasonable grader, and the readings, while long, I thought were more interesting than the ones I've had to read for other LS classes. So knowledgable but doesn't shove it in your face and really likes to hear what we have to say. Take him!!

Vivek is a wonderful professor who truly has a passion for both the course topics as well as a desire for students to engage in meaningful conversations surrounding course topics. If you are interested in the course themes, then this discussion-heavy class is right for you! He also offers support on writing papers and processing your ideas.

Professor Bhatt is the best! Easily the best Global Works professor I have had, and maybe even one of the best at NYU. He is highly knowledgeable, passionate, and caring for his students. The class is 75% discussion, so it is crucial to participate. If you have the chance, TAKE HIM!

Professor Bhatt is genuinely one of my favorite professors I've had at NYU. Extremely intelligent, wants everyone to understand what he does, and encourages questions if you don't. Class is very discussion based, so attendance does really matter, but you'll want to go regardless. Easy to reach, and grades thoughrougly and fairly. Highly recommend!

analysis.name: Vindya  Bhat
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Read off lecture sheets and did not explain concepts well. Condensed material of two midterms into one and rushed new material before exam. Office hours don't help either. Quizzes every class so it is easy to fall behind.

Professor Bhat gives so much work for how little you learn. She tries her best at lectures but most people zone out. Be prepared to learn a lot of the material on your own from the book. She's very helpful one-on-one, but don't expect to learn much during lecture. Also you better know how to code R if you want to have an easy go of homework.

Coursework is weird, personal reflection makes no sense. Classes always run late for 1015 mins. Expect us to follow instructions in emails that *she didn't mention in class* and give unreasonable harsh penalties. My inclass participation was ignored. Appear to be nice, but I do not understand why is it so hard to communicate with her individually

Professor doesn't really seem to know what she is talking about. Reads directly off slides and doesn't do much explanation of anything. Lecture doesn't add anything to just reading the book and the questions you have won't be answered well. Daily quizzes aren't very hard, though. Homeworks aren't graded roughly, but that may just have been my TA.

She seems like a nice person but definitely does not understand linear algebra. It's a beautiful subject but had to rely on MIT's OpenCourseware to understand. Prof. Bhat cannot answer conceptual questions, makes many mistakes even when copying from the sheet she has, and lectures are basically her writing notes down and then reading them back.

analysis.name: Mary Bitel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Not college level teaching. Acting for kindergarten. We have to learn dialogue from scene study but she just says good job and because she is not an actress it is a waste of time. Other teacher section much better use of student energy.

Mary is nice, but her Working with Groups class is so freaking boring. It seems like she says the same main points every class. The final paper is broken into three parts, and due over the course of the semester. There's no way to tell what your grade will be until the end of the semester. She's always willing to help, but the class is boring.

I really liked Mary and her Working with Groups class. The class was interesting and taught me quite a bit that I plan to apply in the future. There's a lot of reading in order to really do well, and sometimes she's not always clear in her lectures. But, she's very accessible to meet with you outside of class if you need more personal help.

As someone who didn't know that much about acting Shakespeare, Mary was INCREDIBLY helpful! She was such a bright and positive force in the classroom, gave great feedback, and challenged my acting skills. Most importantly, she made sure everyone was having fun at the end of the day. HIGHLY recommend taking The Bard Out Loud with her!

I am so angry to find out now that Mary Bitel is away this semester because she is a terrible teacher first of all, she is not a professional actress and I could take this class this semester with a real actor!!!!!! She is a waste of time. She wants every person to like her that is all she cares about.

analysis.name: Kathy Bishop
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 94 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely adore Kathy! She's an amazing professor. The LS curriculum is pretty dull, but Kathy knows how to make history come alive. I'm going to miss office hours in Starbucks. Good luck in trying to enroll in her class; her class fills up quick!

she yaps all damn class its really really boring but shes a diva at times. we read a lot of books and have a group project/presentation which was easy; all tests are online and long answer, we have two big essays she's a tough grader on those; a mix between art history and like literary history; overall class is super easy A take her!!

Her class reminds me of middle school: no space for critical thinking and you are required to memorize everything that has talked about in class, and things she talked about are useless and boring. I bet she knows that her classes are boring so she would force to remember everything she said and test you on these. Complete waste of time and money.

I love Dr. Bishop, her lectures are always interesting and detailed. Had one easy group presentation, two papers, and three tests. Doesn't give the best feedback, but you can always ask her for detailed feedback. Just read the books and look over your notes, and you'll be fine. She really does care about her students, totally would recommend!!

I really adored class with professor Bishop, even when it got lecture heavy. She genuinely wants to see you do well in the class and gives you the test topics (and some of the answers) before the tests. She's willing to change the essay prompts so you can write about what you want. I cannot stress this enough, she is so kind!

analysis.name: Jacqueline Bishop
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She has a really bad attitude & can be really rude at times. We focused on one project all semester which got repetitive and boring. Would not recommend her.

Honestly, I've seen so many horrible reviews of Bishop, but she's really not that bad. If you're willing to show up, participate, and be respectful, you will be fine. She kind of gives high school teacher vibes, so I guess it depends on how you feel about that. Her assignments are interesting, and you can get by without doing most of the readings.

The rubric kept on changing throughout her semester. Learned nothing all semester because she was so unclear with everything. But if you were even a minute late you would be a target. Also is very rude in general, cuts you off mid sentence, does not allow for discussion. Super hard to reach outside of class (has never replied to any of my emails.)

PARTICIPATE AND ATTEND CLASS AS MUCH AS YOU CAN!!! cannot be reached outside of class for anything, also not an understanding teacher. unclear feedback and guidelines. class material is not difficult at all, but she definitely is. take at your own risk and if you do, be on your best behavior.

She will give you comically ambiguous assignment prompts. After you write an essay that satisfies all of the requirements, she will insist that this isn't what she wanted. Submitting a first draft is like opening Pandora's box. I feel like a circus monkey trying to guess what the trainer wants.

analysis.name: Elisa Biagini
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: WREX and WCI were so much fun with professor Biagini! She has a wide variety of assignments in terms of both genre and prompt. Loved how much creative freedom we had in essays and the final portfolio. No final and the midterm is a fun in class essay. Field trips are beautiful and inspiring. Provides good feedback on each piece. Such a fun class!

This class was one you never really had to stress about, and the content was interesting and fun. Her writing prompts are more adventurous and fun than the other writing teachers and she really focuses on our perspectives. I will say, if you are really hoping to improve your writing, this class may not be it, but still a great class and teacher.
I absolutely loved my classes with her. She pushes for participation but it helped me come out of my shell! Would 100% take again. Her assignments and readings are super fun and interesting too!

She is the best writing professor at NYU Florence! I had her for 2 semesters and it was my favorite class. Her assignments are fun and creative, and you can usually pick any topic for your essays (other classes are confined to prompts). On field trips, she brings her puppy, and once she held a movie night at her parents' house. My fave professor!!!

Professor Biagini is the best! She is very kind and helpful. Classes are discussion-based but she allows you to talk about all kinds of important topics through writing. Three essays (three pages single or double spaced), you can choose your own topic and a lot of short writing homework for each class, but it is interesting and doable. TAKE HER!

analysis.name: Bill Rayner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bill Rayner is, by far, the BEST professor I have ever taken with. He is funny, kind, and very knowledgeable on the styles of music he discusses. Both his “Songwriting” and “Creating Music, Composing Worlds” classes focus on music, but you do NOT need to have pre-existing experience beforehand! If you ever get the chance to take with him, DO IT!

He's really sweet and super chill. Just show up to his class and get an A! The purpose of the class is simply to introduce students to guitar and get them excited about playing. Although you won't learn as much from this as you would in an individual session, it's fun and he's just trying to develop student's interest in it so they keep playing.

Bill's a great guitar instructor. He personally cares about the success of each students and breaks down lessons at your pace. The class is structured depending on what you want to learn, and there is a wide variety of topics that Bill is knowledgeable about. Definitely a good instructor for beginners as well.

I love this man with all my heart. I am in his class as i write this. this is my second class with him and I'm so disappointed I don't have another semester to take another class with him!!! billy rock i will miss you

if u take this class PLEASE participate and chat with him! he's so nice :-)

class for all levels, if ur alr skilled he lets you just vibe on ur guitar

analysis.name: Maharukh Bhiladwalla
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 214 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: She does come off very strict and mean, but honestly, I enjoyed her lectures. They were interesting and she gave many examples that I was able to relate to. She did brutally scold me during a one-on-one meeting for "memorizing" my way through the class, and I was very sad :( but afterwards I changed my study methods and improved a lot on exams.

review_highlights.comment: Professor Block is the nicest guy.
