Her online quizzes were almost impossible to get a good grade on, and her attitude was unsympathetic to the status of the world. There were some quizzes, 1 paper, and 2 Tests. She read off her slides mostly, and one class legit just read a research paper outloud.

She is a great TA, and I really got inspired during her lectures to learn more about the topic. However, sometimes she does not really have a lot of patience if you don't understand immediately what she is talking about. She is super knowledgable but other people are not necessarily anthro majors! She is very helpful though and always available!

analysis.name: Antoine Cerfon
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A brilliant Professor. Clear and helpful lectures complemented by his own notes. Exams are not unreasonable and he bundles weekly quizzes together so you only have to deal with them every month or so. Really great guy!

Professor Cerfon is an excellent math professor, he really tries to explain the concepts carefully, gives multiple ways to solve the problems, and is really open to questions both after class and in office hours. He was even willing to talk to me about how I'd learned the material in the past to better teach in the future. Nice review sessions too!

Cerfon is a really good professor. He explains abstract concepts well, and provides very detailed lecture notes (and he tells funny math-jokes in almost every lecture).  Homework is really, really, really hard, but he would help you solve them if you come to his office hours. And he curves the grade pretty generous. Really RECOMMEND his course!

Cerfon is a very good professor in many ways. He explains the material well, and he understands how difficult the material is for students. At the end of the semester, he bumps your entire course grade by 1 letter grade if he sees that you have demonstrated excellent effort. Homework is insanely difficult, but his lecture notes should help.

Antoine is easily one of the BEST Math professors you can find here at Courant. He cares about students' progress and would meticulously explain anything should anyone comes to questions on it during class. Also has a great sense of humor. Could recommend 11/10

analysis.name: Pádraig Cearúil
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Pádraig was my best prof in all of undergrad. He truly gets to know you as a person, is incredibly understanding when personal problems pop up that take precedence, and he cared far more about our passion for the Irish language than our short term retention - he lit a fire in my that will last for a long, long time. Go raibh maith agat a Mhúinteoir

Padraig is the cool Irish dude you never knew you needed in your life. As others have said, he wants you to do well. I forgot what a question word meant on my oral exam, and he skipped the question. Just put in a little effort, and have a little fun. Also, enjoy all the singing. (He does take attendance).

analysis.name: Charles Stine
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Extremely heavy coursework. Far more than the other Algebra sections and even worse than the Honors Algebra class. He seems to be pushing his unreleased textbook onto students this semester as "lecture notes" (which he doesn't even complete in class and we are responsible for learning ALL the content). Notes explain stuff in THE MOST CONFUSING WAY

Great lecturer, very disorganized. Gave us 130 pages of notes the night before the exam, never uploaded homework on time, no clear topic guidelines for the bi weekly recitation quizzes, never replies to emails. Homework would take around 15 hours a week to complete on your own. I'm kind of torn bc he's a very kind person and great at teaching.

One of the best Math professor, delivers very good lecture by explaining all the definition and proofs. Care about students and answer all the questions always extend office hours. Curve the final exam grade so don't be so worried about the grade. Take his course and you will find the charm of Math.

Prof is passionate about the subject and a great teacher. Echoing the prev comment, he was completely irresponsive via email and info about the final was very last minute. Be prepared to spend many hours of the week on HW which will be difficult and even more hours on the tests.

Amazing lecturer who knows his materials. Conveys his ideas very clearly and helps everyone to understand the material. Only downside is the massive amounts of homework, where we are intended to work in groups or else the homework will take over 20 hours per week.

analysis.name: Ranjana Choudhry
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor is not in top of her emails, takes days to respond. Her expectations are unrealistic, two chapters to read each week with about 4 lengthy assignments for each chapter while wanted students to do other work. Gives work just for us to remain busy. She calls out students in front other the other students about why they are late.

2 weeks into this class. just avoid her at all costs. does not reply to email. insane homework load. youre literally gonna be on mcgrawhill doing homework for like 4 hours. just miserable. find another professor unless youre ready to suffer for 4 months. here is your warning

no response to emails even if you have emergency. Does not care about her students. Only picked her because she had no reviews at that time, and since now she does,DO NOT MAKE THE MISTAKE TO CHOOSE HER!

Super engaging lecturer, very accomplished, and very passionate about the subject matter. Lots of homework/group work, but manageable. Always gives detailed feedback. Gets much tougher/more demanding as the course goes on, but it is so worth it.
Do not recommend take this professor.. She doesn't care how hard you try . All assignments are  hard and you can't see the answers too.

analysis.name: Silvia Chegia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Silvia was one of the funniest teachers for my elementary intensive Italian in Florence. She just wanted to hang out and really help us. We would watch movies and sing Italian songs to be better immersed in Italian culture. She spoke only Italian and had us learn by doing, without overcomplicating things. Very flexible and understanding.

The goat of Italian. She was extremely kind, funny, and friendly all the time! She also was a great teacher and her tests were always fair! You can talk to her like a friend about anything and she will be more than happy to engage. Also plans a concert where we get to sing Italian music at the end of the course. An absolutely amazing teacher!
I took her ARMI class last year and really enjoyed it! She is really caring and wants you to truly learn.

analysis.name: Christine Rushlow
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Rushlow teaches well, and her exams are on what she taught. There are no surprises. She assigns quite a few textbook problems early on, and those problems are good practice for the exams, so make sure to do them. She even gives practice exams with problems almost identical to the real ones. There's no excuse to fail unless you're too lazy to study.
Very nice professor! very accessible after class and she was willing to answer all your questions during office hours to make sure you understand it. Highly recommended!

Professor Rushlow's lectures are some of the clearest and most digestible I've encountered at NYU. Her exams are based entirely on what she teaches, without surprises. If you do the homework and attend her lectures, you'll do well. Take advantage of recitations and your TA -- it's much easier to understand the material than it is to memorize it.

One of the best professors I have met throughout my undergraduate studies! She is really brilliant and insightful, and a juggernaut in the fields of genetics. She was one the few professors that I had that accomplished a seamless transition in teaching the course on a virtual platform. I truly wished that she taught another course.

Rushlow really knows her stuff when it comes to genetics, and she was always really helpful during office hours. TAs were also really nice and understanding. Lectures + slides are def a must in order to study for exams. As long as you understand the lectures you'll do fine. Half of the final was just previous Q's taken from previous midterms.

analysis.name: Cindy Chiu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The GOAT. Her lectures are exceptionally well-structured, interactive, engaging, and inspiring. The course itself is extremely practical and useful. The workload is very reasonable. Super chill, kind, accessible, and genuinely cares about her students. One of the best professors I've had!

I took this class with Prof. Chiu two years ago. She is truly a great professor and very knowledgable in her field. The content are well organized and engaging, I also find that the coursework greatly helped me in my internship performance afterwards. Take her if you can! You won't regret it.
Her class is engaging. I would say she is the best professor I met this year. She is truly encouraging and supportive. The class content is well organized in a clear manner. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Burt Goldberg
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 124 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Burt Goldberg is the best professor I've ever had at NYU. Do not believe any negative thing you hear about him. This man will change your life. I love him.

He's really rude and mean to all students. On the first day of chem recitation he said that none of us would ever become doctors, and every class he doesn't fail to brag about his own MD and PhD. Yes, that's super impressive, but he doesn't have to put his students down at the same time. Difficulty doesn't apply because he's giving Halpin's quizzes

Was continually disappointed by his lectures. He does yell a lot and insults people, but as someone mentioned he's a softie, you can see that he means well. At first I liked him, but I learned almost nothing from lecture cause of his rambling; he goes off on a tangent with stories from his youthetc. Which is sad because he's obviously intelligent.

If you took chem/physics back in high school, class should be a breeze. Personally did not go to a class after like the 5th one and am still doing well. Lectures boring, with quizzes. Labs are the hardest part, get to know the TA's and know how to ask for help. Outside of class, prof is super rude/unreachable, though he might just be old/grumpy.

The homework, quizzes, and tests are online and easy as long as you read the textbook, and the TA's and labs are chill and fun, but lectures have almost nothing to do with the material. He is near impossible to reach outside of class, and he goes on massive tangents about how useless our generation is and how we are at fault for society's decline.

analysis.name: Christopher Citera
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Interesting, but lot of notes and information to keep up on. Genuine person and clearly wants to improve the best that he can, as he looks for feedback after every class. There were only two assignments he gave and harshly grades with no chance of extra credit. There's also lecture questions at the start of each class (all on exam which was easy).

MPAVP-UE - 1152 
Professor Citera is such a genuine person. He will seem a little cringy at first, but then you quickly start to realize that his teaching style really works (at least for most people). There was a lot of work for this class, however, that's simply because it's very important information. His call outs are very helpful for me. LOVE!
Long lectures, and random call on questions at the beginning of each week

analysis.name: Andrei Cimipian
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The worst psychology class I've ever taken. He explained things fast (although NOT in depth) and therefore tended to overgeneralize. Confusing wordings of exam questions, never encouraged students to think beyond the lectures (or to raise questions). Not willing to have discussions after class, even when he was obliged to. Plus real bad TA.

I had Professor Cimpian for Intro psych, and given that it was online, I still had a good experience. He lectures are very clear, sometimes a bit fast, so be prepared to take good notes to really help with the exams. He does offer an extra credit opportunity and is always willing to answer questions. Great class, and definitely recommend it.

His lectures are honestly really boring and dense. When he explains things, he tends to overcomplicate. His tests are easy, once you understand how he writes them. His wording can be confusing. But an A is easily achievable. Loved that it was online. He records every lecture so you can go back to it. Talks super fast though.

Solid prof! Concise and digestible slides, zoom vids are posted so you can watch whenever on 2x speed. He posts straightforward review sheets for each exam, and exams have a 3-day period to complete, which is a lifesaver. I didn't find the textbook useful for the exams, but still interesting (and free) to read

LOVED Professor Cimipian for Intro to Psych. Lectures are super clear, interesting, and easy to follow. There are no notes on his slides, so be prepared to take notes. He does go too fast, allows for questions and makes sure everyone is engaged. Literally one of the best professor I have had to far at NYU, never had to worry about  his class.

analysis.name: Cian Dorr
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor, extremely smart and knowledgeable in his field. Open to questions and gives amazing answers. During office hours you can expect to know a lot more beyond the class materials, which is great for any philosophy majors who want to dig deeper into the topics. Very adorable and friendly.

Fantastic professor. It is very inspirational to talk to him, as when you say something that you think is correct but is actually silly, he would still treat it as if it is a serious theory but would then propose a little objection which makes you soon realize that it is wrong. Anyway, it is a pleasure to take his course.

Fantastic Professor. When you say something that seems to be correct but is actually silly, Professor Dorr would still treat it as if it is a serious theory, and then propose a little objection that makes you realize you are absolutely wrong. It is very inspirational to talk to him and be taught by him.

knows a lot about his subject, but cannot teach to save his life. Office hours are unhelpful, slides are unhelpful, readings are disconnected from material, extremely not approachable at office hours.
EXTREMELY difficult for philosophy students who don't have much previous knowledge of Math. Don't come

analysis.name: Nicola Cipani
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cipani is knowledgable and very passionate about his subject. His texts and ideas class was fascinating, and if you pay attention you can get a lot out of it-highly reccomend!! Grading is left up to the TA's, so sometimes its difficult to fully grasp what they want from you, but my TA was pretty accessible outside of class/recitations.

Prof. Cipani is fantastic! Visual Languages of the Renaissance, while sometimes a bit difficult to wrap your head around, has genuinely made me think differently. It sounds insane, but where ever I go, I am much more aware of symbolism in architecture, art, etc. and it has made me more curious about the world. A great elective Italian studies class
It's easy to get a good grade in this class, but way too hard to get an A

This professor is the best; at first, I was a bit lost since it's not a typical class where you will typically understand the reading at first, which is okay since during your recitation, you and the TA will go over it together and it's going to help. There were about three/four mini papers, a page a two, which were helpful for your final essay.

Looooved his class. He takes attendance in the lectures and there's no notes/recordings so it's better to go---sometimes the readings can get overwhelming/confusing but since the professor explains them during lecture it's all good. Really fun recitations and the papers weren't too hard! I liked what we learned too.

analysis.name: Cindy Rodriguez
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's been almost a year since I took Cindy's class and I am so glad I got her early on because not many people know how to teach writing. I had some bad profs since her, so now I can say I appreciate her more now then I did back then. At the time I thought she was giving us too much to do and being too picky; now I know why that was so important.

She's tough. The class started out easy and then became harder. Just when I thought I was getting the hang of it, Cindy (she lets her call her by her first name) pushed us to do more. We created cool news blogs and I'm proud of the work I did in the class. Looking back, I'm really glad I took her section. So much better than the other ones.

Had her for Inquiry. She takes some getting used to, since she doesn't really stick to the syllabus, but she's a really nice person. Brought us pizza because she was happy with our rewrites. She's interested in our progress and wants to see us succeed. I like her way of giving us three big stories, instead of one every week.

This was a tough class. Lots of writing and rewriting. I thought I was a good writer and came to realize I have a lot to learn about journalistic writing. But I feel I learned a lot in this class. She made us create blogs and I am happy with the way mine came out. I have a nice portfolio now, which I will build on.

Professor Rodriguez really worked us hard. Lots of rewriting of our stories, but the assignments were fun and just like she predicted my writing improved 100 percent. She's not like other professors who haven't been in a newsroom in years. She has a ton of experience and it shows in the way she conducts the class.

analysis.name: Eugene Cittadino
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Only take him if you are truly interested in learning more about Darwin/ evolution otherwise this class will probably bore you. This class is heavy reading but lectures are low stress. He requires blog posts which are not graded but will hurt your grade if you do not do them. I feel like he was a fair grader and he gave good feedback on essays.

I wish somebody warned me about Professor Cittadino, probably the worst professor I have had at NYU. His lectures were boring, reading assignments were ridiculously long, and the homework were extremely time consuming. He is a strict and tough grader. He will take off points if he doesn't like your idea and does not allow revisions. Do not take!!!

Eugene is a really kind professor. He obviously is knowledgeable about ecological and environmental history. He connects a lot of the material to his own life, which isn't a bad thing. I enjoyed the range of readings he offered and the class atmosphere. While he grades a bit tougher on papers than other professors I've had, he's still fair.

Definitely a good man who is passionate about the subject, he just is not very open to others people ideas and does not make it clear what he is looking for in his papers. Only consists of 2 fairly short papers and one final research paper. Only take if you are actually interested in the history of disease.

Eugene was a pretty cool professor. He did give a lot of readings, however they were all really interesting and gave different perspectives on environmental thought. I would definitely recommend taking his class!

analysis.name: Marcelle Clements
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This semester is not over yet but I just wanna say that Marcelle is amazing. She could be extremely helpful if you follow all her instructions and read the book.

This year (2013-14) Marcelle was voted one of the best professors in CAS. There is no doubt in my mind that she deserved it. Proust is hard to read, especially for college freshmen, but Marcelle makes it worth it. Come to class, participate (both in class and online), and for the love of god, do the reading, and this class will be rewarding.

My god if only I knew what I was getting myself into! The class was overall fine, but the reading is quite hefty! The readings averaged around 300-400 pages a week, missed my Halloween. The reading is long and a bit boring with occasional times piquing my interests. The writing is fine and fun because you can choose your topics.
Amazing professor, extremely passionate and cares deeply about her student's success
there are a few people in a lifetime that have a dramatic impact on who you become as a person. Marcelle has the potential to be one of those few.

analysis.name: Gian Luca Clementi
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Evil professor, unclear final exam guidelines (most of your grade), you have to participate to get credit in the class. During debates will show a bias to one argument and will actively interrupt you when speaking.

Professor Clementi is passionate about what he teaches. However, he gives unclear guidelines, he overcomplicates easy concepts, and rambles about one or two ideas without reaching the subject matter in the homework (and assigns mountains of readings). He encourages participation but argues with students. He can be disagreeable and rude.
Interesting class, but he ruins anything good about it. He can be very rude and is very biased. You lowkey have to suck up to him and even then he probably will not like you.

The content of this class is relevant and stimulating. The way it is taught is a different story. Clementi is a kind person, but he struggles to present material clearly, which makes lectures confusing. There is also no room for challenging his way of thinking. Finally, the grading criteria are unclear, with little transparency about expectations.

Clementi, Clementi, Clementi, where do I begin? Both exams spread me wide open and made me feel like a sorority girl being passed around a football team. As I flipped through the exam, every question felt like it touched me from inside because I couldn't even write down a word. You better pray to every person you know because it's mostly luck :)

analysis.name: David Clinton Wills
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Definitely not a difficult professor if you're just looking for a good grade, He's nice, and offers availability. However, his class will not teach you very much, both with feedback on papers, and just day-to-day in classes. Every class is pretty much just reading aloud a reading.

For a writing class, there was way too much reading. He was really sweet and genuinely cared about his students, but we didn't get much practice writing. There were only 2 writing projects the entire semester (one being the final, which he didn't even grade). The class environment was nice, but not the best professor for writing.

He is nice & funny, but cold calls constantly, which gets annoying and makes me anxious. If you dont do the readings you will sound stupid when he calls on you. He assigns way too much reading, sometimes multiple at once, often over 25 pages, so the workload gets hectic. Also the readings just don't make sense half of the time, doesn't explain.
Super chill!! Great and laid-back professor. Lots of reading, and every class is entirely discussion-based. You will not learn a lot, but it is an easy A!

Dr. Wills is a very sweet and nice professor who cares about his students. However, I wish that care also went into the course content. The classes were very boring and even though it is a writing seminar don't expect to learn anything about writing. I don't know why I put effort into the papers the grade was based just on grammar and spelling.

analysis.name: Joshua Clayton
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clayton was very kind and knowledgeable. The class consists of lectures where you watch videos beforehand and workshops where you work on coding project. The midterm and final are harder than you'd expect- the final especially was a lot harder and ruined my A in the class so beware. Besides that, very great class, I highly recommend!

Prof. Clayton was wonderful! He gives really good lectures and engages students with the material very well. His homeworks are very helpful for learning and fun to do even though some of them can be a bit long. He allows cheatsheets on all exams, and everything comes from his lectures.

Love this professor! He is super friendly, explains the material well, and is open to helping students. Midterm and final are a bit tougher than you might expect, so study well. Otherwise, the class is pretty easy since he drops lowest homework, quiz grade, and will weigh the final more if you do better on that than the midterm.
prof clayton is a great professor. exams are fairly simple if you learn the class material & use the practice materials. i learned a lot and it was a fun class! def recommend if you need to take ICP.

He's very caring, makes things clear and understandable, and always willing to help. Weekly assignments, but not too bad however he is very nit picky in grading so do everything exactly as it should be done. Test are relatively fair and gives you study guide beforehand. Definitley an excellent teacher! Highly reccomend!

analysis.name: Claudia Lago
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a caring and supportive professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. Although her English isn't perfect, this is a Spanish class, and she created a comfortable environment where everyone can build confidence. Be prepared to participate in class discussions. There is a lot of coursework, there are also pop quizzes and exams.

One of the most respected and best professors in the spanish department, and at NYU. By no means is this a breeze through class, but she is incredibly caring and will give you every opportunity for success. Amazing professor, amazing role model.

Really awesome professor. Keeps everyone engaged during class time, and offers great out of class support. Mindtap / Brightspace Homework for each class, but wasn't difficult. Exams were tough, but as long as you study, you'll be fine. She also gives comprehensive study guides to help you! Definitely recommend!!

Claudia is genuinely one of the nicest professors I've ever had at NYU. You can tell that she's really passionate about teaching and she is pretty clear with her material. There is a fair amount of work for a 6 credit class and the pacing is not too fast. She is very understanding and tries hard to make sure you understand everything.

Claudia is so wonderful. She constantly made our whole class laugh, and before anything, she wanted us to be good friends, learn and have fun. All assignments in Intermediate Spanish I were easy, straightforward and she always had a rubric and clear grading criteria. Online workbook is decent too. Having a Cuban Spanish prof. is the best.

analysis.name: Clara Fernández-Vara
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Very Subjective.She favors certain game genres, and when uninterested, her feedback often focuses on criticism with a dismissive tone, rather than constructive suggestions. 

In our case, she only engaged with 20% of our work before giving a negative evaluation. Although we responded to clarify her questions, she didn't seem open to discussion.
Extremely subjective grader. No grading criteria. If you have any other choice, don't take her course.

She is very flattering to native English speakers and very discriminating against Asians.
If you're an Asian, run! Never take her class! She gave all Asians really low marks.
The specific way she discriminates is: ignore.
You will feel very disrespected in her class.
Clara is a tough grader but you'll be fine if you try your best. As an Asian, I had Clara for two courses but never felt discriminated. She was very nice(at least to me) and I got pretty good grades.

Clara's a tough grader but she knows the specific parameters she wants students to adhere to, and gives clear concise feedback that genuinely helps improve the games you're making. She's accessible outside of class and is genuinely passionate about what she teaches.

analysis.name: Claire de Obaldia
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: French and Expatriate Literature -- Dr. de Obaldia is a sarcastic bully who gaslit me into thinking I couldn't write papers. Several other students noticed that her behavior towards me differed from the rest of the class. Her feedback was limited and unhelpful. Quel dommage !

One of my least favorite professors I've had. Her class is not particularly difficult so I won't say you absolutely shouldn't take it but I do not like her as a person and her feedback was often phrased in a rude way. (and if *I* think she's rude you know it's bad...)

I loved her classes. I felt challenged but pushed beneficially. Content was inspirational and so relevant. Her input and knowledge are so worthwhile. Even if it is a high effort, time-consuming course, I would take it again.

GET READY TO READ!! Will read a lot in this class she comes in class expecting all readings to be completed prior and will drill hard on the reading content. She grades very hard, so if you want to challenge your writing skills, feel free to take the class, but she will give honest (sometimes even rude) feedback on your paper.

If you show up to class, do the readings, participate, and submit the homework on time, you will be golden. Genuinely cares about student's progress and lives and doesn't take BS. Super smart and well-read and really knows what she's talking about. Dr. Obaldia will only have an issue with you if you are a bad student.

analysis.name: Wilmiriam Cotto Castellano
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
She is HANDS DOWN the best Spanish teacher I've ever had, both at NYU and throughout my life. There is clearly a reason why she is the director of the intensive Spanish courses. If you have the ability to take her, do it.

Sincerely, 
Someone who has taken Spanish since 7th grade.

Look, you are taking intensive spanish, its going to be hard, but she brings her dog to class, is very kind, goes over stuff that dosnt make sense the first time, and isnt too tough on grading. you have to try though, if you dont try why are you taking this class. but she is the best, litterly amazballs.

Wilmiriam is literally one of the sweetest and best Spanish professors! She is always willing to help if you are struggling and makes it so exciting to come to class each day. She is also a fair and easy grader and is super patient and caring. Her dog is also so cute!! Definitely take her if you have the chance :)

I've had four Spanish professors at NYU and she is definitely my favorite. She is so caring & kind, no matter how I'm feeling when I come into class I always leave smiling. She is very helpful, encouraging, and understanding. My Spanish has definitely improved with her as a teacher. If I have the opportunity to take a class with again I will!
do not take her elementary intensive spanish...

analysis.name: Clayton Curtis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Brilliant guy, but possibly the worst professor ever. He goes off on useless tangents, claims his tests are based off only the "broad concepts" and then goes onto ask specific, minute details. It's not fair how difficult his class is considering the other cogneuro professor gives open book tests and an optional final. TLDR: Avoid him!

He's so difficult to understand it's like each class is a competition for him to see how much jargon he could pack into it. His slides are literally blank except for poorly labeled diagrams. We're only graded on 5 20 mcq quizzes (1 dropped) and an optional final that's kept even if it lowers our grade. If you take cog neuro DON'T take it with him.

I usually like to focus on the positive things when writing these reviews but like some other reviews, he is unfortunately not a good lecturer. He does ramble a lot and it is quite hard to keep up in order to take notes. He is very knowledgeable by all means, just wish he would switch up his lecture style for the future.

His lectures were pretty loaded with information, and although he definitely knows a lot about his field and knows what he's talking about, he's not very good at explaining coherently. I appreciated his funky humor, and he's very nice, but that's not really enough. You're basically on your own in this class, but if you work hard, you can get an A.

Classes were clear and interesting, however textbook sucked (glossed over complex lingo and said, "we'll discuss what this actually means in chapter 17"). Also, grading was inconsistent and hard, but that had more to do with TAs than prof Curtis. I could never be mad at his cute, bald, Texan self.

analysis.name: Tal Correm
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Correm is a very good professor if you want an easy A. She's very nice and cares about what she's teaching but her lectures can be boring. If you focus sometimes and do some of the readings you can get an A. Shes very understanding about attendance as long as you dont overdo it.

Easy A overall. The class can feel a bit dull and lectures can be hard to follow, but she is very kind and understanding toward students. Exams are open-notes; as long as you attend class consistently and keep up with the work, the course is very manageable.

Lectures whole class except for 15-20 minutes. Chill teacher, extremely well versed in the subject and knowledgable. Pretty caring I think. Lectures quite boring. Reading by the end of the year becomes quite hard and long. Definitely learned some stuff though. Midterm is short answer + MCQ, final is a paper (compare contrast). Two critical essays.

Really nice and sweet woman. Her grading is fairly easy and the workload from the class is pretty chill. Midterm and final are open notes and the two papers in the class were easy to write. Most people ended with an A.
really really nice lady but really really boring lectures, 2 essays + 2 open-note exams, easy A if you pay attention sometimes and know what the readings are about

analysis.name: Joan Connelly
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: loves hearing herself talk, very lecture heavy but slides are not useful for studying. she is inconsiderate of her students, not flexible or understanding even in the case of illness. get ready to study everything on your own.

brilliant woman and somehow has a complete blind spot for basic ideas of learning and teaching. Her lectures are word vomits with attached dates. Convinced she became a professor to dedicate more time to listening to her own voice. 70% of the class failed the first quiz, she blamed us for not memorizing/developing 10 different essays. run away!

This professor is an odd mix of amazing and nice with horrible and mean. If she sees something in you then she will use you, if not you are nothing. She is only out for her own glorification. Although extremely intelligent, she cares more for the stuff she teaches than the students she is teaching. You are not important, its what you can do for her

Few of my professors possessed Dr. Connelly's ability to weave an absorbing, humane narrative from art historical interpretation. She helps students see familiar subjects differently by asking productive, revelatory questions. Her guidance during my research project was meticulous, and demonstrated what it means to be an authority in one's field.

Prof. Connelly is fascinating, articulate and caring. Her Greek vase painting class far exceeded my expectations, in the sense that she made it incredibly fun. I will never look at them the same now, plus I'll never lack the ability to show off in the Greek and Roman art section of museums now.

analysis.name: Timothy Cogley
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Grades depend on three exams with three questions, so no time constraint. The exams are very similar to the optional practice questions, so do them! The only downside is that because the exams are a bit easier, the econ curve is competitive. Also, going to class is a must because he explains the concepts clearly.

Explains everything in detail. Class is very straightforward. Exams are graded harshly so understand the methodology for every concept, and explain your economic intuition clearly. No hws, however practice problems given every week, which you must do for the exams. Also, there was no curve down and the TAs are very helpful.

The professor is a funny guy and presented the materials in a clear way. The slides he provided are well-designed and the lectures were inspirational. If you come to the lecture and finish the practice questions he provides with, you will get a solid A. The exams are quite similar to the practice questions.
A humorous guy and a lovely professor. No homework, and hard work pays off.
Horrible person. TA's even worse.

analysis.name: Conor Creaney
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I found Conor to be a very chill and kind professor. He clearly cared about your work and wanted to help you personally improve as a writer. His feedback was often helpful and specific, while also respecting how personal most essays could be. I found some of the readings to feel a little useless and random, but overall enjoyed coming to his class.

Conor is the best. Gives lots of reading and takes some time to give feedback but is really understanding of deadlines and gives you an A if he sees effort/improvement throughout your drafts. He's just a funny nice Irish guy and I learned a lot in his class.

He was genuinely such an amazing professor and person. It's really easy to just talk to him about anything during classes. He is really lenient to getting assignments in on time and won't really take points off.

Conor is a sweet and quirky man, very flexible for deadlines. Take him if you want to become a better writer, otherwise it's too much work for the uninterested-i found it quite rigorous for a required course. His feedback is vague yet demanding, the other reviews are accurate. His teachings ended up being fundamental for all my writing since then

Conor Creaney is a nice guy, but his classes are very boring. I watch the clock every time I go to his class. He takes your phone away from you & gives you a ton of things to read for hw. His essay topics are not clearly structured and when students asked him to be more clear about the prompt he was not helpful at all. He's a tough grader as well.

analysis.name: Susan-Sojourna Collier
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Sojo has genuinely changed the course of my college and professional career within the first semester of my freshman year. She is so energetic and passionate about everyones work. I truly look forward to seeing her and getting feedback in class because everyone feels so safe and excited to work in her class. Cannot rec her enough. Tough love!

Prof. Sojo is deeply dedicated to developing strong writers. I took her class two years ago, and even though I was no longer enrolled with her, she graciously offered to read my Intermediate Narrative script. She provided detailed notes on each draft, and she even met with me over the phone during the summer to help me strengthen the story.

Professor Sojo's class was the highlight of my week and something I always looked forward to every Wednesday. She creates such an engaging, supportive, and inspiring environment that makes learning both fun and meaningful. Having her as a professor has been an absolute pleasure, and I hope to take her in the future.

Professor Sojo's Storytelling Strategies class was a highlight of my semester. I've always struggled to call myself a writer, but her class gave me confidence and new tools I'll carry forward. She made screenwriting approachable and enjoyable, with contagious energy and a truly welcoming environment

This is my second time taking her class & I wld take her a 3rd time if I could. She really took time with me to make sure my short film script was strong and impactful. She read several drafts - gave me detailed notes and met with me after class. She is very dedicated to everyone 'living their lives like it's golden' (one of her fav sayings).

analysis.name: Marie Cruz Soto
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took Boundaries and Transgressions, the workload wasn't overwhelming, the topics covered by the course were compelling, getting a good grade is realistic so long as you complete the readings and attend class. However, Marie would commonly arrive to class 10-15 minutes late, wasn't very accessible via email, and grading often wasn't very clear.

Boundaries and transgressions IDSEM- definitely not what the description said. Nice professor but goes off on tangents a lot and doesn't really accept another viewpoint other than her own. Some readings are confusing but it's not that hard to participate in class if you do the readings. Very discussion based, one project, no papers

Loved Prof. Marie Cruz Soto! Definitely thought the readings were unexpected at first but it all came together in the end. Definitely reccomend, part of you grade comes from attendance and particiaption but there are no tests! But the main part of the class is just how interesting the the discussions are.

Coming from a public school, most of the concepts discussed, such as Jacques Lacan's mirror stage and the abject in reference to Kristeva, were challenging and difficult to grasp at first. But Professor Cruz Soto is very engaging, understanding, and informative. As long as you do most of the readings and add to class discussions, you will be fine.
I love Professor Marie Cruz Soto. Her mind is so powerful and beautiful. Expect to read a lot because that is the only way you will learn. What you put in is what you get out of the class.

analysis.name: Jonathan Corcoran
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The best professor I have took this semester. Clear and organized tutorial structure for the whole semester, and the writing plan for the course is carefully planned. From exploring yourself to the whole society, three essays are very helpful. Professor Corcoran is very nice, the vibe of the class is chilling and comments for essays are useful.

Professor Corcoran deserves all the 5/5 he can get!! If you have the chance, PLEASE TAKE HIM!!! Only 3 essays for the whole semester, with workshops within the classes. The readings he gave were all so interesting and I never felt bored in that class at all. Participation was 25% of the overall grade. Wish I could take him again!! Such a sweet guy!

GOAT of LS writing profs. Literally all you have to do is turn in 3 essays, plus sit there for 3 hours each week without going on your phone. If you can do that, you WILL get an A. His stories are also super cool and he is just a genuine and kind guy. Can't recommend him enough tbh

Professor Corcoran is amazing, he's rated 5/5 so many times for a reason. There were only 3 big essays in this class and a few short papers that we wrote in class. There is reading due every class, but it consists of interesting articles and leads to stimulating in-class discussions. He is chill, just make sure you get to class on time!
I would vehemently defend professor Corcoran against any potential 4/5 rating, he deserves every single 5/5. A caring, warm-hearted professor you should take, an easy A but you learn so much too!

analysis.name: John Crawford
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The only Camera 1 professor to take if you are serious about learning about cinematography. Unbelievably knowledgeable about the physics, technology, and craft of cinematography down to the minutia, but does not expect you to know ALL of it to get an A. Incredibly hardworking, dedicated, and passionate. An honor to learn from him!

John is an exceptional film theory professor.  His knowledge of the medium of film is extensive and he's very willing to help you outside of class.  I have gone to him several times for assistance with projects and he's answered my questions every time.

Had him for Camera 1 and I learned more in his class than any other class at NYU so far. He is so intelligent and in my opinion, hilarious. My roommate thinks I'm in love with him (I probably am) because I'm always telling her how amazing he is.

Simply the best!!! THE BEST TEACHER IN FILM... you will learn more than in all your other classes combined. (I saw that nobody had rated him in a while and thought it needed to be said that he has maintained his awesomeness over the years)

John Crawford is not only incredibly smart, but he is also very interesting. John Crawford taught me more in one marathon lesson than I had ever learned before about the tech of film. Also, he looks like Jesus and has the same initials.

analysis.name: Denise Cruz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: super easy A impossible to get below an A- to be honest, but very boring and you do not learn anything. her classes are mandatory for the csd major so consider them a grade booster but I have never see anyone really pay attention to her lectures.

Professor Crus has truly been the best professor I've had at NYU so far. Her lectures are very straightforward. Once you get to know her, she is very caring and funny. You can tell she wants you to do well in the class. The exams and quizzes are super easy, but still make sure you study. It would take a lot of effort to do bad in her class.

Prof. Cruz was incredible! Such a sweet and caring professor that was also very knowledgeable. She really wanted her students to succeed and gave a lot of opportunities for extra credit. There are a lot of quizzes/tests/assignments, but she offers generous deadlines and gives you good guidance on what material to study for. TAKE HER CLASS!

OMG, I love Professor Cruz, I would take the class again just because I like her so much, She has so many funny stories and she truly loves what she does, the class itself was not bad at all, mostly online quizzes and interesting lectures. I'd pick her as my favorite professor, if you get her you're lucky
Very accommodating and understanding professor. She genuinely wants you to succeed in her courses and in the field, she is an absolute gem.

analysis.name: Cristina Beltran

she's very sweet and likes when people participate. the class is easy, but a lot of reading. you can easily get away with looking over the slides and studying by going back to specific parts of the reading, I do recommend reading since it just makes it easier (just skim it). The tests are super easy and she gives you the test questions beforehand.

3 Exams + Oral Final

Gives study guide with exact questions that will be on tests, just memorize your answers.

Exams have a time crunch only because of hand written answers that require 1-3 blue book pages.

You don't need to read anything imo, very chill class. Lovely teacher but class is super slow if people don't talk. Moderately interesting.

great professor!!! content was so interesting and engaged the class, also enjoyed the recitations. midterms and final were very easy because she gives you the a list of potential questions before the exam and an easy final project too. defo recommend.

Just a ridiculous amount of reading—around 90 pages a week and they are dense. And all she does is go over the same readings in class. Easy tests but it's unreasonable to expect students to be able to do all of it in 4 days when you have other classes. Also she is extremely politically biased—even for me who actually agrees with her points

analysis.name: Crystal Parikh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I learned a lot from this APA cultures course, the content is incredibly important and interesting. Graded by a wide variety of assessment formats including papers, worksheets, class participation, group work, discussions. This course demanded a lot of my time, must stay on top of readings and lectures because of random comprehension checks.

Super sweet, quite understanding, but class is kinda hard to follow: we jump around quite a bit from culture to culture/timelines with no through line, makes it hard to memorize info. Lecture is fine, readings are lengthy but skimmable (you'll do fine on exams even without reading, w/ study guide). recitations are boring and unnecessary imo.

I've heard she's great for her other courses, but I have absolutely hated this class. It may be because this was her first time teaching it. It is an enormous amount of reading per week and a skim over them in lectures. In her lecture she shows how intelligent she is, but she rambles and never finishes a sentence and I always leave feeling confused

The most disorganized prof I have ever had. She speaks at a million miles per minute with no clear direction. She often interrupts her own thought with a different thought and never finishes a sentence. I use to go to every class but I stopped going altogether, as you can never decipher what she's saying. What's the point? Should not be a professor

Professor Parikh is kind, caring, and funny. She makes a point to learn her students names. She is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the subject. Her class (Reading Race and Representation) is well-organized and reading heavy. However, she does not have absurd expectations and the class is manageable. There are about 6 essays, and a final.

analysis.name: Cris Beam
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a great professor that taught me more about writing in one sem than all four years of high school. Readings and essay prompts are intimidating but she does a great job at making them approachable. The writing workshops are so helpful and she really expands the way you think about writing. She challenges you but in a way that you learn from.

Cris is an absolutely phenomenal professor. The self is a very intimate class and she was very good at making it a safe space. She is dedicated to every student, actively responds to emails, and will definitely help you grow as a writer. She's also not afraid to let a tangent go which makes every class feel better than the last.

I adore Professor Beam! She is so kind and welcoming and treats everyone like writers. Super non intimidating and really improved my writing. Grading wasn't harsh which allowed room to really work on just becoming a better writer. It may take a second to realize her genius, but once you do the class really grows on you! Recommend this class.

There are a lot of readings, but as long as you read it a bit and participate, you should be fine. The essays are pretty straightforward, and she is a generous grader. Overall a very kind and amazing professor :)

Definitely one of my favorite professors of all time. As the other reviews state; sharp, fun, inspiring, and knows her stuff. Super available to students. Wants to see you succeed. Had her for book and magazine editing. Will be taking her again for creative non fiction. William Paterson University.

analysis.name: David Cregar

The only thing that made his class even bearable was the hot girl sitting next to me. Unless you have lots of oxy to get high on during his class, you would probably want to hang yourself during his class

Professor Cregar's assignments are quite vague. He usually gives u only a direction and that's pretty much it. He taught me more how to think as a writer than how to write well and he taught students a lot of useful tools. He is accessible outside classroom and is not a tough grader as long as you figure out what he wants( which is not easy.
Very unclear about what he wants. His classes are interesting, but he never gives clear answers in feedback. Respects students but not an easy grader.

analysis.name: Chiara Curtoni

review_highlights.comment: So funny and cares a lot about her students. She genuinely wants you to succeed. So funny and smart, I don't have a bad thing to say about this woman.

I loved taking Chiara Curtoni for Intermediate Italian 1. She is great at explaining concepts and knows when people are struggling and how to make it clearer for them while creating on-the-spot problems and examples. She is really sweet and at the end of the semester the class feels like a fam. She wants you to succeed and to learn.

She definitely has high expectations, but also wants her students to succeed. While this class was one of the more difficult classes I've taken at NYU, I learned a lot and improved my Italian immensely. Class is fun and engaging, with lots of discussion. Not an easy class, but a very rewarding one if you have the time for it.

Loved Professoressa Curtoni! She's great. I took her for Advanced Review. Her class was not overly difficult, but she was a bit harder on the grading for essays, but nothing crazy. Would def recommend!!

analysis.name: Barbara Perez Curiel
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is the best professor I've had. Makes learning Spanish really easy and she is super understanding. For an Intensive Class, she surely made it a really easy class. There is a lot of homework, but she is really understanding when it comes to deadlines or lateness. It is better to take Spanish Intensive then Intermediate 3.

Barbara is the best!! Learning a language is hard in itself and your success is reflected by the amount of work you put in. Needless to say, she was an amazing professor. She graded very leniently and I looked forward to going to this class even though it was at 9:30 a.m. every day.

The course is hard because of the work load and level. But professor Curiel is an amazing teacher. She was always accessible, timely with feedback and created a very inviting atmosphere for us to participate. She genuinely helped us learn the hard concepts and was always open to questions. She is the best teacher to have for difficult subjects.

she's so sweet and fun and very understanding!! grade is based on 3 tests, 2 in-class essays (which you can re-write for a higher grade), vhl homework, oral assessment, and participation. the coursework is not that hard and the tests are exactly like the practice tests.

Intensive summer course over zoom, still very enjoyable despite the two hours in front of the screen. Very interesting class and readings and brought up a lot of theoretical and historical perspectives I had never heard before. A lot to read but prof was understanding when we couldn't finish everything and would work with us from there

analysis.name: Nicole Cuddeback
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A good teacher who clearly cares about her students but her guidelines and expectations for assignments can often be unclear or unspoken causing mistakes. She allows you to self-assess yourself but the grade she gives you can be influenced by the tiniest of things you don't remember. She is very passionate and engaging but her grading can be weird.

A great teacher who provides detailed feedback and is always available outside of class to offer additional comments and guidance for revising essays. She is knowledgeable about writing and goes above and beyond to help her students improve. The journaling activities she assigns are helpful for developing writing skills and self-reflection.

Professor Cuddeback is my favorite teacher in NYU Florence. she's a chill teacher, she allow us to do the self evaluation for our midterm and final grade. I really enjoy our class discussions, which are open and encourage us to express our thoughts freely, while she skillfully expands on our ideas. she also really care about student, shes brilliant

I thoroughly enjoyed Mrs. Cuddeback's ACA course. Mrs. Cuddeback is a thoughtful and supportive teacher who provides detailed, constructive feedback to help you refine your work and create the best possible paper. Her dedication to her students' success made the experience incredibly rewarding. Would definitely take again!

Anyone who has made a living writing in Florence, Italy is worth your time. She helped us all explore our personalities through writing, in a creative workshop, and then we sat together to discuss contributions on a blanket in the grass beneath the most beautiful architecture in Europe. Perhaps I even carried some Chianti in my backpack.

analysis.name: Cynthia Melendez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 2 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: take this for intensive, lots of work but thats all the intensive courses, very good professor and caring

Such an understanding and lenient professor, easy grader if you show up and participate, and the class has so many assignments that it's hard to genuinely get a bad grade. If you have to take intensive Spanish, take her class!

analysis.name: Cyrus Mohebbi
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor will randomly pick your grade after not returning any assignments, then when asked for clarification fails to have records of any specific assignment grade. Also chooses to follow the stern curve even though its an elective grad course. Not afraid to fail people. None of this would be a problem if the course material wasn't super easy.

Great experience with Cyrus, very caring prof. Will take time to listen to you, re explain lectures and answer questions even mid lecture. He requires participation and attendance but fair grading and does everything he can to help you succeed. Cyrus is also pretty funny and laid back, he is easy to talk to and sympathetic.

Disorganized course with unclear expectations. The syllabus lacked detail on grading, and criteria were never clearly explained. Attendance is strictly enforced, and missing one class can seriously hurt your grade. Heavy reliance on a curve made grading feel opaque and stressful.

The class is tough, but Cyrus is anything but. He is caring, funny, and engaging. He tries to make the material relevant and easy to understand, especially for those who aren't familiar with it. He's clear with grading and provides ample opportunities to learn and reach out if you're struggling. Would definitely take again!

One of the most confusing classes I've taken. Assignments and grading standards weren't clearly explained, so it was hard to know how to do well. Attendance was enforced harshly, which added constant pressure.

analysis.name: Cynthia McCallister
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Took her the last semester of my undergraduate. The least I can say is that she severely stressed me out. Her guidelines were very unclear, her syllabus was a mess, and it seemed like she was just winging it every class. She was not open to feedback and would always blame everyone else instead of taking accountability.

Genuinely THE WORST professor I've ever had. She makes constant changes to the syllabus about IMPORTANT things and DON'T TELL US, only telling one student and expecting it to trickle down. No accountability, heavy victim mentality, and overall pretentious mess that can dish but can't take. NYU needs to be held accountable; paying for THIS is wild.

Did not learn anything this entire semester. I wouldn't even call her a nice person because she's a typical white woman asserting her savior complex on the educational narrative. Once asked how to handle gang fighting in schools, she avoided my question entirely. Focused on saying environments dont shape kids, they shape who they are, even as teens

(pt.2) She literally used AI to write her emails to us. She didn't know how mass emailing worked and blamed it on us. She trauma dumps anytime the class is upset with her teaching and scheduling style. Frankly, she needs to be fired. She committed a micro-agression the first day she saw me. Oh, she also used AI to write her books...we had 2 read it

Worst professor I've had. She heavily encourages AI use & admitted multiple times her inability to complete basic tasks without it. Does not teach in the slightest. She just leaves you in groups the entirety of class to discuss middle school level youtube videos or her projects, which are poorly explained & assigned with extremely tight turnaround.

analysis.name: Brian Culver
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 96 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the best teachers hands down, he really tries to be mindful of people with different viewpoints and doesn't just support one. You should definitely take, he gives out the final before and other than that it's mainly 3 essays and they're very interesting to write about and easy to get done in the time he gives to work on them.

I have no idea what kind of right mind would give this professor a 5/5. He is a nightmare please just trust  me. I trusted the rate my professor rating and took his class. Now in all honestly I never want to learn this subject every again. If you wana ignore this and take his class? Be my guest. Just don't come crying after, saying I was right.

I loved having him! He's really big on class engagement, but he honestly makes it really easy to participate. You're literally given the discussion questions beforehand so that you can prepare. We were assigned 4 essays, each worth 20% of our grade. He's pretty fair with grading, but feel free to visit his office hours for help. Would recommend!

Really nice guy but sometimes he makes comments that translate very poorly or can be distasteful. Lectures are engaging, with lots of art and literature analysis. TAKE NOTES!!!! Essays are based on things he says explicitly in class. However, essays have no rubric, so go to office hours for help or questions because he will help!

Despite asking the silliest questions on class, he graded papers very harshly by making deductions for super minor details that he has never clarified when assigning them. Very rude during office hours and replying emails.  Maybe your grade heavily depends on whether he likes you.

analysis.name: Cynthia Allen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
