review_highlights.comment: She is my adviser and my professor, and I think she's fantastic. In her "Digital Art & New Media" class we learn about all kinds of cool stuff and go to really cool and informative things around the city. She is kind, funny, and very interested in the subjects. There is regular homework, but it's more than manageable.

I have to be honest, cynthia is a really nice professor and she means well. However, I think that the course work can be pretty dated for a new media class, and the topics discussed stay very surface area. As a student in this class, I would have liked to learn more and stay concentrated on more relevant topics.

Digital New Media class.  Class was interesting, cool field trips.  Must do readings and blog about them, but we never spoke about them in class. Blogging was annoying but class is easy and interesting.

digital new media; lectures very little, shows short movies and brings in lecturers a lot (professionals from the field). has lots of connections; takes us to the galleries in soho/chelsea. the only work you have to do outside of class is keep a blog about the class & some dinky timeline, which is really easy. class is long, though but also easy.
If you are into comics this is a must take. Cynthia is very flexible, fun and helpful. She is a great teacher.

analysis.name: Cyrus R.K. Patell
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Patell is a joy to watch in lecture. For someone constantly preaching about "cosmopolitanism", he doesn't seem open to listening to other perspectives and definitely gives the impression that he thinks he's better than everyone else. Generally really interesting lectures though.

One of the most intelligent, interesting, engaging and funny profs I've had. A ton of reading and in-depth analysis, but it's worth it. He makes even the boring material interesting and nuanced, and integrates modern media into class in a fun way. His lectures are well-structured and coherent. I recommend to all English majors!

Professor Patell is a sweet and funny guy who clearly cares about what he is teaching. I took Cosmopolitan Imagination, for a core class, It was quite difficult. The context was very philosophical and required 100+ pages of reading every night.

He's an absolutely amazing teacher. He uses all sorts of media (Star wars clips, anyone?) to explain difficult concepts. Every day as class starts he plays music associated with that day's lecture. He makes learning entertaining. I can't count how many times we all cracked up in his class. Not that it isn't hard- the homework load is insane (2 days to read a novel..) but it's worth it to have him as a teacher. A+++

I've had Professor Patell for both ConWest and Writing NY. Though I found him incredibly intimidating for a time, a meeting with him during office hours completely changed my view. He is consistently brilliant, an engaging and passionate lecturer, a fair grader, and an unrelenting advocate of discourse.  Highly recommended!  Hope to have him again!

analysis.name: Cyrus Patell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cyrus is my academic mentor and lit professor. His phenomenal classes on the epic and drama traditions give you the cultural foundation to appreciate art and life more critically. That being said, the workload for his class is quite heavy; 100+ pages reading/ class, submitted 100+ pages of notes + two 10-paged essays for the sem.

Whoever rated this guy 5 stars must love reading. I have never been in a more difficult class in my life. This man does not seem to understand what is reasonable amount of work to assign full-time student. 1 complicated book a week + addtl readings, one quiz on the book at the top of class, weekly assignments, tri-weekly essays, films 🤦🏻

I took his Global Shakespeare class. It took me a while to warm up to Patell just because of how we were kind of thrown into the course with having to read one Shakespeare play a week and submit responses to them. Its also a really discussion driven class. Final project was actually a ton of fun, though the 8 page final paper was not as fun.

Took him last semester for Technophilia and Its Discontents (Texts & Ideas) and I literally wish I could take the class again. I have never attended lectures for a class that were more interesting and worth listening to than his. Honestly the best class I've taken here at NYU and I miss it so bad.

If you can understand what he says then you might as well consider not doing college entirely. I have not met a professor who is so unclear in his speech, yet so proud in it. 

I think he has some trauma from being an immigrant and never quite fitting in during English class. Believe me, I am one too.

analysis.name: Aurora Czegledi
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor was terrible. She yelled at you for asking students next to you for help during class. She posts homework assign. online every so often, but doesn't inform you. Good luck checking everyday to realize no homework is due til the one day you miss and it's past due. She doesn't teach much. Interview final midterm homework and class part.

Worst teacher I have ever had. Showed up to every class, participated like crazy, tried as hard as I could. When she gave me a C for my final grade, she told me I put no effort into the class. Ugh. Plus she never teaches. She just reads out of a book. I'm posting this just so no one else has to suffer through an awful semester with this teacher.
I knew more spanish before this course than I do now.

analysis.name: Cynthia Thompson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Please do not mistake my rating for a 1. It is actually a zero. The reviews on this page are so misleading it's criminal. She literally never shows up to class, so imagine our disappointment waking up for an 8 am, going to class, and then just leaving 30 minutes later. Work is brainless. Learned nothing. Avoid her class at all costs. Waste of money

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! She didn't show up to four classes in a row in person, and even when we went online (bc of corona), she was still 35 minutes late. She doesn't tell you in advance when she doesn't show up either, so she completely wastes your time. Her essay topics aren't that interesting. She also brags about herself a lot too

Her class is honestly super interesting. We have amazing readings and great discussions. She loves when you participate and attendance is mandatory. Super helpful if you visit her during office hours with your paper. She also lets you do multiple drafts if you didn't do so hot the first time. Genuinely wants to help you!

Super nice and entertaining!  I personally don't think she's a tough grader, just follow directions on assignments and you'll get an A.  Sometimes vague, but you still do some fun and interesting stuff in class.  Definitely recommend.

She's always late for classes, and she canceled classes frequently. She either tells us an hour before the class or after class. There was at least one time that we waited for her for half an hour in the room and she didn't show up. Our class is 8 AM! Never get feedback from her. Only had two writing assignments so far. Lots of forums and readings.

analysis.name: Enrique del Risco
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Enrique was such a nice professor, he genuinely cares about his students and tries to teach in a fun way. There were 3 exams a few papers with homework assignments and a presentation. The class was not hard, just had to put in some work in. There are going to be 3 classes per week so a little bit more workload.

If you just want to be done with your foreign language requirement, Enrique is amazing. I never understood his accent, didn't go for 80% of the classes, or submit my project, and basically gave up halfway through the semester. But Enrique understands, and Enrique saves your freaking hide. Not the hero I deserved, but boy was he the hero I needed.
I really love this professor, if you have to take spanish please take him he is the best

Cool guy! He has a thick Cuban accent but you'll get used to it. He cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. Prepare yourself for full language immersion. He doesn't speak English but can understand it. There is a lot of homework. It's not necessarily hard, but you will have homework and readings three times a week. Vale la Pena!

Enrique is an amazing guy, he treats you like a friend. He loves everything related to history and Latin America, he is really passionate about it. Lots of HW, and projects, but hey this is a course for natives. Do the projects and participate, don't worry much about HW, but READ ALL the texts from the syllabus. He is pretty clear on what he wants.

analysis.name: Denice Martone
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Really really good professor. Very accessible outside class, caring and inspiring. She helps me a lot during one to one conferences. Really nice professor. Not a hard grader. If you put effort in writing, you will get a pretty good feedback. Would definitely take her class again if possible!
Favorite prof in my first semester in NYU. She is so nice, and help me a lot with my intellectual thinking process .

She is very approachable and easygoing though she sometimes leaves a first impression of sternness...She is not strict on deadlines which is rather important in courses like writing the essay. Try to be nice with her and she will show her nice part. A good friend.

Actually if I had another chance I would want to try another professor, but Dr. Martone is definitely a good professor. She really inspired me during classes. She has a really high standard, so prepare to see some unpleasant grades.

A very nice professor. I like her very much. The deadline she posted on the syllabus is not the final deadline. She may change the deadline after she reads our essay. She also gives recommendations to our drafts, so we can make it better.

analysis.name: Christina Dehaven
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Christina is so amazing! You receive so many invaluable resources from her Producing a Short Screenplay class. She's easily accessible outside of class and just a very kind and caring person.

The lectures were all so helpful and informative and the projects actually help you learn. Highly recommend taking her if you get the chance!

If you hate this woman you are probably a psychopath, because she is honestly the sweetest person ever. I've never met a better professor than Christina. She is EXTREMELY organized, always on top of things, gives thorough feedbacks and has organized so many resources for us to utilize for the rest of our lives. AND she genuinely cares about us.
Kind, respectful, passionate. A great example of how competent nyu tisch teachers can be.
Maybe the sweetest professor alive. So knowledgeable and caring. LOVE HER!

She gives you resources you will use for life! Im producing a film because she allows students to pitch their ideas. The film I'm producing for is no longer taking her class and still uses her google drive! LOVE HER! CANNOT RECOMMEND MORE

analysis.name: Debraj Ray
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Tough class, but the Professor is a great lecturer and makes complex topics easy to understand. The problem sets are quite difficult, but are important to understand for the exams. Accessible outside of class. I missed an exam due to a personal issue and he was very helpful in trying to accommodate me on a short notice.

I was the worst student in his class. Missed the first midterm, did poorly on the 2nd, did ok on the finals, and somehow he still gave me a passing grade. For people who show up to class, he always try to make sure we understand before moving on. Course material is definitely hard, but the negative reviews about his character are not justifiable.

Extremely rigorous and demanding course, but also one of the most intellectually rewarding classes I've taken. If a negative review is based solely on strict grading, I don't think that's a fair reason. I didn't do well in this class, but that does not take away from the fact that Professor Ray is a truly dedicated and thoughtful instructor.

One of the best econ professors I've had. Homeworks are hard and so are the exams. But he teaches very well and if you study hard, you'll understand the concepts. Also, go to office hours. It definitely helped me.
eye-opening course but very difficult. problem sets and exams are difficult, one of the harder courses I have taken at nyu

analysis.name: Deborah Williams
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO. NOT. TAKE. She won't agree w any opinion that doesn't align w her own & refuses debate against her opinions. She gives extremely bad feedback trying to get u to rewrite ur paper to align with her ideas. I've never met a prof w such an active interest in verbally diminishing her own students. if u value ur mental health at all do NOT take her.

DO NOT TAKE. My commons had been removed 3 times, yet I am still here to common. DO NOT TAKE. She is trying to implant her ideology into you, and if you don't accept it, you end up with bad grades and attitudes. Grading also doesn't make sense. I was fooled by the high rate of commons to take her class. Please trust me, DO NOT TAKE

Professor provides unclear instructions, grades extremely based off of subjectiveness, and is extremely stubborn. Would not ever take again, please don't take this writing course, choose someone else if they are avaliable. Not to mention the amount of essays you have to write.

Grading is very subjective. You don't know what she wants to see. If you happen to match her ideas, the score will be high, but if not, you will get the lowest score. That doesn't happen if you put the same effort in other professor's class. If you have to take her class, you should talk to her more to guess what opinions she wants to see.

Criteria are extremely vague—three lines of text, leaving you unsure of what she wants. She offers chances for revisions, but her feedback only consists of marking everything as "unclear and confusing." Even if you revise and clarify everything she suggests, the shockingly low grade—unlike anything you've received in other classes—doesn't improve…

analysis.name: Judy Del Giudice
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took acting 1 and it was great. There was a lot of effort and participation required for the class but overall had a very fun time. Judy is a great acting teacher. Be ready to step outside of your comfort zone.

Acting II(open arts): She is nice and friendly but treats the class as if it is for majors. Very tough grading, especially since the class is designed for little/no experience. If you are a good actor, take the class and you might enjoy it. If you are casual, avoid this professor. Her exercises are useless. You might learn some minor techniques.

I took Acting II with Judy, and absolutely loved her! She's had a considerable amount of experience in the acting world, and, as an experienced actor myself, I really admired her. She's definitely your typical zany theatre teacher, but she's great and loves her students. Not to mention the class is a blast! I highly recommend this class.

Judy is incredible! I took her for Acting I and Acting II and she was consistently great. The only thing that changed was my grade. I got a B in Acting I because I rarely went and an A in Acting II. My advise, take her, go to the class, participate in her fun little activities and you will get an A. It's a fun, exciting class!

Judy is a great and enjoyable lady. She does pick favorites, and makes it clear who they are. The exercises are fun, but repetitive and boring in the end. She grades Acting I way too harshly, and doesn't explain why. Her enthusiasm  is beautiful, but If you're looking for an easy A - forget it.

analysis.name: Rena Deitz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: very accessible outside of class. your grade is split evenly between many assignments. lots of group work. super kind and caring prof. i've taken two classes with her and would recommend both. you'll learn so much!

Great professor, super clear expectations, always happy to talk outside of class, generous with extensions. Show up to class on time, try not to miss too many days, do class readings, and put some effort into papers and you should be good.
Great professor overall, will to get to know each student and help those who need it, easy class overall.

She a nice and sweet person, but she makes the class feel pointless. No one except me and two other people participate, and the room is dead and silent. The workload is alright, there is an insane amount of reading, but you don't need to read it to participate in class. I wouldn't take her class, boring, and a waste of time.

This course is reading heavy, but they aren't mandatory. Reading the intro & conclusion is sufficient enough for discussion, and Professor Deitz summarizes the information really well in class. She actively engages the students to participate in class. I recommend attending her office hours to discuss your assignment ideas as she gives good advices

analysis.name: Dean Lennert
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dean taught an amazing Action Analysis 1 class. I learned so much through his feedback for not just my own work but his feedback on everyone else's too. Super sweet and accesible outside of class. You won't want to pass up an opportunity at being his student if you're an animator.

Although Dean can give hard-hitting homework, it is what you'll want and need as an animator in order to advance within your craft. With a lawful good personality, Dean is available outside of classes to give critiques on drawings and independent critiques separate from class work. He is willing to extend dates and overall wants to see you improve.

Dean is willing to extend deadlines, hand out As, and is willing to look at ALL your work. He gives great feedback and EXISTS for you to grow as an animator. He's always really smiley and he's been super accomodating during the pandemic. I would take him multiple times if I could cause he's that good. I've grown so much because of him. Great guy!

Dean is *amazing*. I have never met a teacher so willing to offer help outside of class. Go to office hours!!! Dean will make sure you get feedback on anything from career to work. He is incredibly talented and knowledgeable. It is clear he really enjoys helping his students.

analysis.name: Anita Dhir
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Never understood what she wanted. She expects students to know words and phrases that she should be teaching. Her classes are all over the place. She constantly has students learn concepts themselves & then present them. I understand she tried to make the class Agile, but I don't think it worked. Probably one of my most infuriating professors

Never, never take her class! All course materials were sent via email and she always needed to correct herself several times. Poor PPTs -- some words are even placed out of the page and when she sent the pdf to me, I can't even see those words. No homework feedbacks, only grades. And the phrase she most often says is 'do not send me the email!!!'

My experience is unfortunately fully in line with the other review here.
I attended the Risk and Change Management course at NYU. There was no textbook, no hand-outs, and no PowerPoints. The lack of materials made the course seem very unstructured, and it made studying for exams extremely difficult.
worst instructor I've ever encountered

analysis.name: Michelle Dent
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amy Hosig is definitely one of the best professors in WTE, take her class instead of this teacher

She is very strict regarding class manners. Never be late to class, don't ditch classes, do your work on time, and don't fall asleep in class. If you get on her good side, expect a wonderful, fun class for the rest of the semester; But if you get on her bad side.. well, say good bye to your A, and you will have to endure her death glares every day.

Prof Dent, though being friendly, can be extremely tough on grading. You should only write things she likes, or you get a C. Classes are boring with no value, she only asks you to read your essays awkwardly in front of all your classmates instead of analyzing the words she assigned. Tons of assignments. Don't take her class!
Professir Dent seems to be wired or mean at the first class, but actually she does not perform that way. Overall she is friendly while the load of hw is kinda heavy.

Professor Dent is responsible and warm. She gives clear feedback and is willing to help you with your personal life problems. She listens to students' suggestions and gives clear rubrics for every grading item. Participation and attendance matter, however. Be sure you contact her each time you are going to be late and be active in class.

analysis.name: Peter Diamond
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is such a hard grader and legit will say one thing pulled your grade down and bump you down a whole letter grade. Super harsh and even if you go to office hours and talk to him about things he wont give you a good grade. Mid term and final are so hard you have to like idenitfy quotes he selected out of past reading and explain. DO NOT PICK

Very nice guy, sweet older man, but definitely more of a traditional style of teaching. Extensive readings, although this whole course is heavy on it. My main complaint is that his grading scheme is very confusing, and apparently he starts all students' participation grades out at a B, but doesn't tell you that unless you ask

He was the worst for Global Works. He absolutely killed my interest in the field of philosophy. He's an EXTREMELY harsh grader and has no good things to say about you. His class was not enjoyable what so ever, as it was the same boring format every day. He makes you feel like an idiot.
Prof Diamond was very nice, though I did find it hard to engage in his class at times. He's also a bit of a strict grader, but his lectures were planned out well. I would go to his office hours!

Just signed up for his Social Foundations for the 3rd semester. Great professor and most intelligent man! He is full of great ideas - i have learned so much in his class. He relates everything to current day events. His voice is really soothing so sometimes you feel the need to fall asleep but just wake up and enjoy his insight! 100% recommend!

analysis.name: Lindsey Dietschi
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I think Professor Dietschi is a good professor in terms of her feedback and knowledge. My biggest issue in this class, though, is the lack of transparency and clear guidance in the grading rubrics. Communications is a very subjective course in and of itself, and the grading in this class heavily reflected that.

Avoid taking her class if possible. While she may seem nice initially, her grading is exceptionally harsh and lacks transparency. She provides no details on participation grades (which heavily impact your final score), and leaves you completely in the dark about your progress. If your goal is an A, choose a different professor.

her grading is so random you will never know how you are doing in the class but at least you can just chatgpt everything and do just as well as everyone else. group projects are so useless and if your teammate doesn't do anything, tough luck bc she doesn't care and everyone in the team will get the same grade. her lectures make me regret waking up.

Very chill professor. Her grading criteria isn't super clear sometimes and she takes points off for random stuff on presentations. However, she is willing to help outside of class and values participation. The class is graded by 2 individual writing assignments and 3 group projects. Overall, a solid choice for Org Comm.

Professor Dietschi is very kind and cares about her students. My only issue is that the grading feels abstract, and it's hard to know where you stand throughout the semester. Even with extra credit, it's tough to tell how much it helps. Great professor, but the grading could be better. I really tried my best :(

analysis.name: Dicky Yangzom
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: LOTS of reading--she'll want you to read 300 page books for homework. The texts she assigns us have the potential to be interesting, but they are very dense texts and she does little in class to help us understand them. She's also extremely standoffish. Don't enroll in this class if you think you can get by by doing the bare minimum.

F&P is a sociology course that barely talks about fashion. sadly prof. yangzom doesn't focus most subjects surrounding contemporary fashion or related issues around the world we're living in now until the last 2 lectures when she'll about sustainability whatsoever. what is "the system"??? Agreeing to the point that she is extremely unapproachable.

The class often begins with rapid-fire questioning at 8 a.m., when many students are still waking up and adjusting. The chain of “why this?” and “why that?” questions can feel overwhelming. It often feels as though we are expected to guess the exact answer she has in mind. This makes participation feel stressful rather than constructive.

A fashion THEORY class and not what people usually picture when they imagine a fashion class. The class itself was sorta drag to get through but she's very intelligent. She cares deeply about her students but not many make an effort to reach out so not many people know that. 

Big exams were online, pop quizzes were annoying but manageable.

I loved what I learned, but compared to other discussion-based classes, classmates agreed she wasn't great at facilitating conversation, especially for ppl new to the vernacular of fashion and already nervous about voicing their opinion. She's probably a great fit for grad students, but not great for an undergrad elective. Never replied to emails..
